title.zh: 卷四百二十四 列傳第一百八十三 陸持之 徐鹿卿 趙逢龍 趙汝騰 孫夢觀 洪天錫 黃師雍 徐元杰 孫子秀 李伯玉
title.en: Volume 424 Biographies 183: Lu Chizhi, Xu Luqing, Zhao Fenglong, Zhao Ruteng, Sun Mengguan, Hong Tianxi, Huang Shiyong, Xu Yuanjie, Sun Zixiu, Li Boyu
title.raw: 卷四百二十四 列傳第一百八十三 陸持之 徐鹿卿 趙逢龍 趙汝騰 孫夢觀 洪天錫 黃師雍 徐元杰 孫子秀 李伯玉 Volume 424 Biographies 183: Lu Chizhi, Xu Luqing, Zhao Fenglong, Zhao Ruteng, Sun Mengguan, Hong Tianxi, Huang Shiyong, Xu Yuanjie, Sun Zixiu, Li Boyu

sentences.zh: 陸持之 徐鹿卿 趙逢龍 趙汝騰 孫夢觀 洪天錫 黃師雍 徐元傑 孫子秀 李伯玉

translations.literal: Lu Chizhi, Xu Luqing, Zhao Fenglong, Zhao Ruteng, Sun Mengguan, Hong Tianxi, Huang Shiyong, Xu Yuanjie, Sun Zixiu, and Li Boyu
translations.idiomatic: Lu Chizhi, Xu Luqing, Zhao Fenglong, Zhao Ruteng, Sun Mengguan, Hong Tianxi, Huang Shiyong, Xu Yuanjie, Sun Zixiu, and Li Boyu

sentences.zh: 陸持之

translations.literal: Lu Chizhi
translations.idiomatic: Lu Chizhi

sentences.zh: 陸持之，字伯微，知荊門軍九淵之子也。

translations.literal: Lu Chizhi, styled Bowei, was the son of Lu Jiuyuan, who had served as prefect of Jingmen.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Chizhi, whose courtesy name was Bowei, was the son of Lu Jiuyuan, former prefect of Jingmen.

sentences.zh: 七歲能爲文。

translations.literal: At seven years of age he could compose literary pieces.
translations.idiomatic: At the age of seven he could already write essays.

sentences.zh: 九淵授徒象山之上，學者數百人，有未達，持之爲敷繹之。

translations.literal: Jiuyuan taught disciples atop Elephant Mountain; the students numbered several hundred, and when any had not understood, Chizhi would expound and clarify for them.
translations.idiomatic: When Jiuyuan lectured on Elephant Mountain to several hundred students, any who failed to grasp a point would have it explained by Chizhi.

sentences.zh: 荊門郡治火，持之倉卒指授中程，九淵器之。

translations.literal: A fire broke out at the Jingmen prefectural seat; in the emergency Chizhi directed the response from mid-course, and Jiuyuan came to value him highly.
translations.idiomatic: When fire struck the Jingmen prefectural compound, Chizhi took charge amid the crisis with steady judgment, and Jiuyuan thereafter regarded him with great esteem.

sentences.zh: 韓侂胄將用兵，持之憂時之懌，乃曆聘時賢，將有以告，見徐誼于九江，時議防江，持之請擇僚吏察地形，孰險而守，孰易而戰，孰隘而伏，毋專爲江守。

translations.literal: When Han Tuozhou was about to launch a military campaign, Chizhi, troubled by the complacency of the age, then went about visiting eminent men of the time intending to offer counsel; he met Xu Yi at Jiujiang. At the time the discussion centered on defending the Yangtze; Chizhi requested that subordinate officials be chosen to survey the terrain—which points were perilous and should be held, which were easy and suited to attack, which were narrow and fit for ambush—and that defense not be confined solely to guarding the river.
translations.idiomatic: As Han Tuozhou prepared for war, Chizhi, alarmed by the era's complacency, set out to seek counsel from leading scholars of the day. At Jiujiang he met Xu Yi, who was then debating how to defend the Yangtze. Chizhi urged that staff be sent to survey the terrain: which positions were defensible, which favored attack, which narrow passes suited ambush—and that strategy not be reduced to river defense alone.

sentences.zh: 具言：「自古興事造業，非有學以輔之，往往皆以血氣盛衰爲銳惰。

translations.literal: He set forth in full, saying: "From antiquity, whenever great undertakings were launched, unless learning assisted them, success and failure often turned on whether one's vital spirit was vigorous or spent."
translations.idiomatic: He spoke at length: "Since antiquity, great enterprises undertaken without the support of learning have usually risen or fallen according to whether one's vital spirit was keen or spent."

sentences.zh: 故三國、兩晉諸賢，多以盛年成功名。

translations.literal: Therefore the worthies of the Three Kingdoms and the two Jin dynasties for the most part achieved fame and success in the prime of life.
translations.idiomatic: That is why so many eminent men of the Three Kingdoms and the two Jin eras won their renown in the vigor of youth.

sentences.zh: 公更天下事變多矣，未舉一事，而朝思夕惟，利害先入於中，愚恐其爲之難也。

translations.literal: Your Lordship has witnessed more changes in the affairs of the realm than most; before you have even undertaken a single initiative, you ponder it morning and evening, with advantage and harm already settled in your breast—I fear it will be hard for you to act.
translations.idiomatic: You have seen more turns of fortune than most men, yet before you move you weigh every matter day and night, with gain and loss already fixed in your mind. I fear that will make decisive action difficult.

sentences.zh: 」誼憮然。

translations.literal: Yi was disconcerted.
translations.idiomatic: Yi was left unsettled.

sentences.zh: 又之鄂謁薛叔似、項安世，之荊謁吳獵，爭欲留之，尋皆謝歸。

translations.literal: He next went to Ezhou to call on Xue Shusi and Xiang Anshi, and to Jingzhou to call on Wu Lie; each in turn pressed him to stay, but before long he declined and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: He then traveled to Ezhou to visit Xue Shusi and Xiang Anshi, and to Jingzhou to see Wu Lie. All urged him to remain, but he soon took his leave and returned home.

sentences.zh: 著書十篇，名《戇說》。

translations.literal: He composed ten treatises entitled Blunt Discourse.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote ten essays collected under the title Blunt Discourse.

sentences.zh: 嘉定三年，試江西轉運司預選，常平使袁燮薦於朝，謂持之議論不爲空言，緩急有可倚仗。

translations.literal: In the third year of Jiading he sat for the Jiangxi Transport Commission's preliminary examination; the Ever-Normal Commissioner Yuan Xie recommended him to the court, stating that Chizhi's arguments were not empty words and that in urgency or crisis he could be relied upon.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiading year 3 he entered the Jiangxi transport circuit's preliminary examination. Commissioner Yuan Xie recommended him to court, declaring that Chizhi's counsel was never mere rhetoric and that in crisis he could be depended upon.

sentences.zh: 不報。

translations.literal: No response was received.
translations.idiomatic: The court took no action.

sentences.zh: 豫章建東湖書院，連帥以書幣強起持之長之。

translations.literal: Yuzhang established the East Lake Academy; the successive circuit intendants, by letter and gifts, pressed Chizhi to head it.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuzhang founded the East Lake Academy, the circuit authorities repeatedly urged Chizhi, with letters and gifts, to serve as its head.

sentences.zh: 嘉定十六年，甯宗特詔持之秘書省讀書，固辭，不獲。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year of Jiading, Emperor Ningzong issued a special edict summoning Chizhi to study at the Secretariat, but he firmly declined and could not be refused only with difficulty.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiading year 16 Emperor Ningzong specially ordered Chizhi to read at the Secretariat. He refused steadfastly, yet could not ultimately escape the summons.

sentences.zh: 既至，又詔以迪功郎入省，乞歸，不許。

translations.literal: Once he had arrived, another edict appointed him a Di Gong Lang within the Secretariat; he begged to return home and was not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: After he arrived, a further edict enrolled him in the Secretariat as a Di Gong Lang. He petitioned to go home and was denied.

sentences.zh: 理宗即位，轉修職郎，差幹辦浙西安撫司，以疾請致仕，特命改通直郎。

translations.literal: When Emperor Lizong took the throne, he was promoted to Xiuzhi Lang and assigned as an aide in the Zhexi Pacification Commission; on grounds of illness he requested retirement, and was specially ordered promoted to Tongzhi Lang.
translations.idiomatic: When Lizong succeeded to the throne, Chizhi was promoted to Xiuzhi Lang and posted as an aide on the Zhexi Pacification Commission. Citing illness, he sought retirement and was specially advanced to Tongzhi Lang.

sentences.zh: 所著有《易提綱》、《諸經雜說》。

translations.literal: Among his writings were Essentials of the Changes and Miscellaneous Expositions on the Classics.
translations.idiomatic: His works included Essentials of the Changes and Miscellaneous Expositions on the Classics.

sentences.zh: 徐鹿卿

translations.literal: Xu Luqing
translations.idiomatic: Xu Luqing

sentences.zh: 徐鹿卿，字德夫，隆興豐城人。

translations.literal: Xu Luqing, styled Defu, was a native of Fengcheng in Longxing.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Luqing, courtesy name Defu, came from Fengcheng in Longxing circuit.

sentences.zh: 博通經史，以文學名於鄉，後進爭師宗之。

translations.literal: Broadly versed in the classics and histories, he was famed in his district for letters; younger scholars vied to take him as their master.
translations.idiomatic: Deeply learned in the classics and histories, he won literary renown in his home district, and younger scholars competed to study under him.

sentences.zh: 嘉定十六年，廷試進士，有司第其對居二，詳定官以其直抑之，猶置第十。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year of Jiading, in the palace examination for jinshi, the examiners initially ranked his policy response second; the reviewing officer, because of its bluntness, suppressed it, yet he was still placed tenth.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiading year 16, at the palace jinshi examination, the examiners first ranked his policy essay second. The reviewing officer lowered it for its blunt tone, yet he still finished tenth overall.

sentences.zh: 調南安軍學教授。

translations.literal: He was appointed instructor at the Nan'an Military School.
translations.idiomatic: He was posted as instructor at the Nan'an military school.

sentences.zh: 張九成嘗以直道謫居，鹿卿摭其言行，刻諸學以訓。

translations.literal: Zhang Jiucheng had once been banished to the region for his upright conduct; Luqing gathered his words and deeds and had them carved at the school for instruction.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jiucheng, exiled there for his integrity, became a model Luqing commemorated: he collected Zhang's words and deeds and had them inscribed at the school as a moral lesson.

sentences.zh: 先是周惇頤、程顥與其弟頤皆講學是邦，鹿卿申其教，由是理義之學復明。

translations.literal: Earlier Zhou Dunyi, Cheng Hao, and his brother Cheng Yi had all lectured in that prefecture; Luqing renewed their teaching, and thereby the learning of principle and righteousness shone forth again.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Dunyi, Cheng Hao, and Cheng Yi had once taught in that prefecture. Luqing revived their instruction, and the study of moral principle flourished again.

sentences.zh: 立養士綱條，學田多在溪峒，異時征之無藝，農病之，鹿卿撫恤，無逋租者。

translations.literal: He established regulations for nurturing scholars; much of the school land lay in stream gorges, and in former times collections had been made without measure, to the farmers' harm—Luqing soothed and cared for them, and none fell behind in rent.
translations.idiomatic: He drew up rules for supporting students. Much school land lay in mountain valleys, where collectors had once levied without limit and farmers had suffered. Under Luqing's care, no rent went unpaid.

sentences.zh: 其後盜作，環城屋皆毀，惟學宮免，曰：「是無撓我者。」

translations.literal: Later bandits rose; the houses round the city were all destroyed, but the school alone was spared, the raiders saying, "These are not our adversaries."
translations.idiomatic: When bandits later ravaged the district and burned the town around the walls, the school alone was left untouched. "These are not our enemies," the raiders said.

sentences.zh: 辟福建安撫司幹辦公事。

translations.literal: He was summoned as an aide in the Fujian Pacification Commission.
translations.idiomatic: He was recruited as an aide on the Fujian Pacification Commission.

sentences.zh: 會汀、邵寇作，鹿卿贊畫備禦，動中機會。

translations.literal: When bandits arose in Ting and Shao, Luqing assisted in planning defenses and struck the opportune moment every time.
translations.idiomatic: When banditry broke out in Ting and Shao, he helped plan the defense and each move proved timely.

sentences.zh: 避寇者入城，多方振濟，全活甚衆。

translations.literal: Those fleeing the raiders entered the city; he relieved them by many means and preserved a great number of lives.
translations.idiomatic: Refugees flooded the city; he organized relief on many fronts and saved countless lives.

sentences.zh: 郡多火災，救護有方。

translations.literal: The prefecture suffered many fires; his rescue measures were well ordered.
translations.idiomatic: Frequent fires struck the prefecture, yet his firefighting measures were always effective.

sentences.zh: 會都城火，鹿卿應詔上封事，言積陰之極，其征爲火，指言惑嬖寵、溺燕私、用小人三事尤切。

translations.literal: When fire broke out in the capital, Luqing, answering the imperial summons, submitted a sealed memorial, saying that the utmost of accumulated yin had taken fire as its sign, and he pointed especially to three matters: bewitchment by favored minions, drowning in private pleasures, and employing petty men.
translations.idiomatic: After a great fire in the capital, Luqing submitted a sealed memorial in response to the emperor's call. He argued that extreme yin had manifested as fire, and singled out three evils: the sway of favored minions, indulgence in private pleasures, and the rise of petty men.

sentences.zh: 真德秀稱其氣平論正，有憂愛之誠心。

translations.literal: Zhen Dexiu praised him, saying his tone was even and his argument upright, with a sincere heart of loyal concern.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen Dexiu praised his even temper, upright argument, and the sincere loyalty behind his words.

sentences.zh: 改知尤溪縣。

translations.literal: He was transferred to serve as magistrate of Youxi County.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to magistrate of Youxi County.

sentences.zh: 德秀守泉，辟宰南安，鹿卿以不便養辭。

translations.literal: Dexiu, as prefect of Quanzhou, summoned him to serve as magistrate of Nan'an; Luqing declined on grounds that it would be inconvenient for supporting his mother.
translations.idiomatic: When Dexiu became prefect of Quanzhou he invited Luqing to serve as Nan'an magistrate. Luqing declined, saying he could not neglect his mother's care.

sentences.zh: 德秀曰：「道同志合，可以拯民，何憚不來？

translations.literal: Dexiu said, "Our ways agree; you can rescue the people—why hesitate to come?"
translations.idiomatic: Dexiu said, "We share the same path. You can relieve the people's suffering—why hold back?"

sentences.zh: 」鹿卿入白其母，欣然許之。

translations.literal: Luqing went in to inform his mother, who gladly consented.
translations.idiomatic: Luqing told his mother, who gladly gave her consent.

sentences.zh: 既至，首罷科斂之無名者，明版籍，革預借，決壅滯，達冤抑，邑以大治。

translations.literal: Once he had taken office, he first abolished levies without proper name, clarified household registers, reformed advance collections, cleared backlogs, and brought grievances to light; the district was greatly well governed.
translations.idiomatic: On taking office he abolished unnamed levies, clarified household registers, ended advance collections, cleared backlogged cases, and heard suppressed grievances. The county was soon well governed.

sentences.zh: 德秀尋帥閩，疏其政以勸列邑。

translations.literal: Dexiu soon became circuit intendant of Fujian and memorialized his administration to encourage the other counties.
translations.idiomatic: When Dexiu became Fujian circuit intendant, he memorialized Luqing's policies as a model for neighboring counties.

sentences.zh: 歲饑，處之有法，富者樂分，民無死徙。

translations.literal: In a year of famine he handled relief with method; the wealthy were glad to share, and the people neither died nor fled.
translations.idiomatic: During famine he managed relief systematically. The wealthy willingly contributed, and the people neither starved nor fled.

sentences.zh: 最聞，令赴都堂審察。

translations.literal: When his outstanding record was reported, he was ordered to the Secretariat for examination.
translations.idiomatic: His excellent record reached the court, and he was ordered to the Secretariat for review.

sentences.zh: 以母喪去。

translations.literal: He left office on his mother's death.
translations.idiomatic: He left office to observe mourning for his mother.

sentences.zh: 詔服闋赴樞密稟議，首言邊事、楮幣。

translations.literal: An edict summoned him, after mourning ended, to report to the Bureau of Military Affairs; he spoke first on frontier affairs and paper currency.
translations.idiomatic: When mourning ended, an edict summoned him to the Bureau of Military Affairs. He opened with frontier policy and paper currency.

sentences.zh: 主管官告院，幹辦諸司審計司。

translations.literal: He served as director of the Office of Credentials and as an aide in the Office for Auditing the Various Bureaus.
translations.idiomatic: He served as director of the Office of Credentials and as an aide in the Office for Auditing the Various Bureaus.

sentences.zh: 故相子以集英殿修撰食祠祿，又幫司農少卿米麥，鹿卿曰：「奈何爲一人壞成法。

translations.literal: A former chief minister's son held a stipend as a compiler in the Hall for Assembling Excellence while also assisting the Vice Minister of Revenue in grain and wheat; Luqing said, "How can we ruin established law for one man's sake?"
translations.idiomatic: The son of a former chief minister drew a stipend as a Hall for Assembling Excellence compiler while also assisting the Vice Minister of Revenue on grain affairs. Luqing protested: "How can we break established law for one man's benefit?"

sentences.zh: 」持不可。

translations.literal: He held to his refusal and would not yield.
translations.idiomatic: He stood firm and would not yield.

sentences.zh: 遷國子監主簿。

translations.literal: He was promoted to registrar of the Directorate of Education.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to registrar of the Directorate of Education.

sentences.zh: 入對，陳六事，曰：「洗凡陋以起事功，昭勸懲以收主柄，清班著以儲實才，重藩輔以蔽都邑，用閩、越舟師以防海，合東南全力以守江。

translations.literal: Appearing before the throne, he set forth six matters, saying: "Wash away vulgar mediocrity to raise up achievement; make rewards and warnings clear to recover the sovereign's grip; fill the upper ranks with men of real talent; weight the frontier commissions to shield the capital; employ Fujian and Yue river forces to guard the sea; unite the full strength of the southeast to defend the Yangtze."
translations.idiomatic: At court he presented six reforms: purge vulgar habits to restore effective government; clarify rewards and punishments to recover imperial authority; fill high office with men of real ability; strengthen frontier commands to shield the capital; deploy Fujian and Yue naval forces against coastal threats; and concentrate the southeast's full strength on Yangtze defense.

sentences.zh: 」上皆嘉納。

translations.literal: The emperor praised and accepted all of them.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised and adopted them all.

sentences.zh: 改樞密院編修官，權右司，贊畫二府，通而守法。

translations.literal: He was made a compiler at the Bureau of Military Affairs with acting authority in the Right Office; he assisted in planning for the Two Offices, penetrating yet observant of law.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed compiler at the Bureau of Military Affairs with acting authority in the Right Office, assisting both bureaus with insight while holding to the law.

sentences.zh: 會右史方大琮、編修劉克莊、正字王邁以言事黜，鹿卿贈以詩，言者並劾之，太學諸生作《四賢詩》。

translations.literal: When the Right Historian Fang Dacong, the compiler Liu Kezhuang, and the proofreader Wang Mai were dismissed for their remonstrances, Luqing presented them with poems; the critics impeached him together, and the students of the Imperial Academy composed the Four Worthies Poem.
translations.idiomatic: When Right Historian Fang Dacong, compiler Liu Kezhuang, and proofreader Wang Mai were dismissed for speaking out, Luqing sent them poems of solidarity. Critics impeached him as well, and Imperial Academy students composed the Four Worthies Poem in their honor.

sentences.zh: 知建昌軍，未上，而崇教、龍會兩保與建黎原、鐵城之民修怨交兵，鹿卿馳書諭之，斂手聽命。

translations.literal: He was appointed prefect of Jianchang, but before he had taken up the post, the two guards of Chongjiao and Longhui and the people of Jianli Plain and Iron City, nursing old enmities, fought one another; Luqing sent a hurried letter to admonish them, and they folded their hands and obeyed.
translations.idiomatic: Named prefect of Jianchang before he had reported, he found the Chongjiao and Longhui guards and the people of Jianli Plain and Iron City locked in vendetta warfare. He sent an urgent letter of admonition, and both sides submitted.

sentences.zh: 既至，則寬賦斂，禁掊克。

translations.literal: Once he had arrived, he lightened taxes and levies and forbade extortion.
translations.idiomatic: On arrival he eased taxes and forbade extortion.

sentences.zh: 汰贓濫，抑強禦，恤寡弱，黥黠吏，訓戍兵，創百丈砦，擇兵官，城屬縣，治行大孚，田裏歌誦。

translations.literal: He eliminated corrupt and superfluous officials, curbed the powerful, comforted the weak and orphaned, branded crafty clerks, trained garrison troops, built the Baizhang stockade, chose military officers, walled the subordinate counties, and his administration won broad trust; in field and lane they sang his praise.
translations.idiomatic: He purged corrupt officials, restrained the powerful, aided widows and orphans, branded deceitful clerks, trained garrison troops, built Baizhang stockade, selected capable officers, fortified subordinate counties, and won such trust that farmers sang his praise in the lanes.

sentences.zh: 督府橫取秋苗斛面，建昌爲米五千斛。

translations.literal: The commandery requisitioned an extra grain levy on the autumn crop; Jianchang was assessed five thousand hu of rice.
translations.idiomatic: The commandery imposed a supplemental autumn grain levy; Jianchang was assessed five thousand hu of rice.

sentences.zh: 鹿卿爭之曰：「守可去，米不可得。

translations.literal: Luqing contested it, saying, "The prefect may go, but the grain shall not be had."
translations.idiomatic: Luqing objected: "Let the prefect leave office, but this grain will not be surrendered."

sentences.zh: 」民恐失鹿卿，請輸之以共命。

translations.literal: The people, fearing to lose Luqing, asked to pay it themselves to fulfill the order.
translations.idiomatic: Afraid of losing him, the people offered to pay the levy themselves.

sentences.zh: 鹿卿曰：「民爲守計則善矣。

translations.literal: Luqing said, "It is well that the people think of their prefect."
translations.idiomatic: Luqing said, "It is good that you think of your prefect."

sentences.zh: 守獨不爲民計乎？

translations.literal: Should the prefect alone not think of the people?
translations.idiomatic: But should the prefect not think of the people?

sentences.zh: 」卒爭以免。

translations.literal: In the end he contested until the levy was remitted.
translations.idiomatic: He argued until the levy was withdrawn.

sentences.zh: 召赴行在，將行，盜發南豐，捕斬渠首二十人，餘不問。

translations.literal: Summoned to the traveling palace, as he was about to depart bandits rose in Nanfeng; he captured and executed twenty ringleaders and did not pursue the rest.
translations.idiomatic: Summoned to the traveling court, he was about to depart when bandits rose in Nanfeng. He seized and executed twenty ringleaders and let the rest go.

sentences.zh: 擢度支郎官兼右司。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Director of Revenue with concurrent service in the Right Office.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Director of Revenue with concurrent duty in the Right Office.

sentences.zh: 入對，極陳時敝。

translations.literal: Appearing before the throne, he laid bare the abuses of the age to the utmost.
translations.idiomatic: At court he exposed the age's abuses without reserve.

sentences.zh: 改侍右郎官兼敕令刪修官，兼右司。

translations.literal: He was made Vice Director of the Right Office with concurrent duty as reviser of edicts and ordinances, still holding the Right Office.
translations.idiomatic: He became Vice Director of the Right Office, concurrently revising edicts and ordinances while retaining his Right Office post.

sentences.zh: 鹿卿又言當時並相之敝。

translations.literal: Luqing again spoke on the abuses of concurrent chief ministers at the time.
translations.idiomatic: Luqing again denounced the abuses of concurrent chief ministers.

sentences.zh: 宰相以甘言誘鹿卿，退語人曰：「是牢籠也，吾不能爲宰相私人。

translations.literal: The chief minister tried to win him with honeyed words; Luqing withdrew and told others, "That is a cage— I cannot be a chief minister's private man."
translations.idiomatic: The chief minister tried to win him with smooth words. Luqing later told others, "That was a cage. I will not be any chief minister's private man."

sentences.zh: 」言者以他事詆鹿卿，主管雲台觀。

translations.literal: Critics slandered him on other grounds, and he was made director of the Yuntai Observatory.
translations.idiomatic: Critics attacked him on other grounds, and he was sidelined as director of the Yuntai Observatory.

sentences.zh: 越月，起爲江東轉運判官。

translations.literal: Within a month he was raised again as transport judge of Jiangdong.
translations.idiomatic: Within a month he was restored as Jiangdong transport judge.

sentences.zh: 歲大饑，人相食，留守別之傑諱不詰，鹿卿命掩捕食人者，屍諸市。

translations.literal: In a year of great famine men ate one another; the acting prefect Bie Zhijie concealed the facts and would not investigate; Luqing ordered the arrest of those who devoured human flesh and exposed their corpses in the market.
translations.idiomatic: In a year of terrible famine people ate one another. Acting prefect Bie Zhijie concealed the horror and would not act. Luqing had cannibals arrested and displayed their corpses in the market.

sentences.zh: 又奏援真德秀爲漕時撥錢以助振給，不報。

translations.literal: He also memorialized that when Zhen Dexiu had served as transport commissioner he had allocated funds for relief, but received no reply.
translations.idiomatic: He also memorialized that Dexiu, as transport commissioner, had once allocated relief funds—a precedent the court ignored.

sentences.zh: 遂出本司積米三千余石減半賈以糶，及減抵當庫息，出緡錢萬有七千以予貧民，勸居民收字遺孩，日給錢米，所活數百人。

translations.literal: He then drew on three thousand-odd shi of grain accumulated in his own office, halved the price for sale, reduced interest at the pawn office, and disbursed more than seventeen thousand strings of cash to the poor; he urged residents to take in abandoned infants and daily supplied money and grain, saving several hundred lives.
translations.idiomatic: He then released more than three thousand shi of office grain at half price, cut pawnshop interest, and distributed over seventeen thousand strings of cash to the poor. He urged families to take in abandoned infants and supplied daily rations, saving hundreds of lives.

sentences.zh: 宴集不用樂。

translations.literal: At banquets he used no music.
translations.idiomatic: He held no music at his banquets.

sentences.zh: 會岳珂守當塗，制置茶鹽，自詭興利，橫斂百出，商旅不行，國計反屈于初。

translations.literal: At the time Yue Ke was prefect of Dangtu and commissioner for tea and salt; he pretended to enrich the state while levying ruthlessly on every side; travelers ceased to pass, and state revenue in fact fell below what it had been at first.
translations.idiomatic: Yue Ke governed Dangtu and controlled tea and salt, claiming to enrich the state while extorting on every side. Commerce stalled and revenue actually fell below earlier levels.

sentences.zh: 命鹿卿核之，吏爭竄匿。

translations.literal: He was ordered to audit Ke's accounts; the clerks scrambled to flee and hide.
translations.idiomatic: Luqing was ordered to audit Yue Ke's accounts. Clerks fled and hid.

sentences.zh: 鹿卿寬其期限，躬自鉤考，盡得其實。

translations.literal: Luqing extended the deadline, personally traced and examined, and fully obtained the truth.
translations.idiomatic: Luqing extended the deadline, investigated personally, and uncovered the full truth.

sentences.zh: 珂辟置貪刻吏，開告訐以罔民，沒其財，民李士賢有稻二千石，囚之半歲。

translations.literal: Ke had appointed grasping clerks and opened channels for informers to deceive the people, seizing their property; the commoner Li Shixian had two thousand shi of rice and was imprisoned for half a year.
translations.idiomatic: Ke had appointed rapacious clerks and encouraged informers to seize people's property. Commoner Li Shixian, who held two thousand shi of rice, was imprisoned for half a year.

sentences.zh: 鹿卿悉縱舍而勸以其餘分，皆感泣奉命。

translations.literal: Luqing released them all and urged them to share what remained; all wept and obeyed his command.
translations.idiomatic: Luqing freed them all and urged the wealthy to share their surplus. They wept and obeyed.

sentences.zh: 珂罷，以鹿卿兼領太平，仍暫提舉茶鹽事。

translations.literal: When Ke was dismissed, Luqing was concurrently put in charge of Taiping while temporarily overseeing tea and salt as well.
translations.idiomatic: When Ke was removed, Luqing was concurrently placed over Taiping and temporarily charged with tea and salt affairs.

sentences.zh: 弛苛征，蠲米石、蕪湖兩務蘆稅。

translations.literal: He relaxed harsh levies and remitted the reed tax at the Mizhou and Wuhu offices.
translations.idiomatic: He eased harsh exactions and abolished reed taxes at the Mizhou and Wuhu offices.

sentences.zh: 江東諸郡飛蝗蔽天，入當塗境，鹿卿露香默禱，忽飄風大起，蝗悉度淮。

translations.literal: Locusts in the Jiangdong prefectures blotted out the sky; entering Dangtu territory, Luqing burned incense in silent prayer, and suddenly a great wind arose and the locusts all crossed the Huai.
translations.idiomatic: Locusts darkened the sky across Jiangdong. As they entered Dangtu, Luqing prayed in silence with incense burning. A sudden gale rose and drove them all across the Huai.

sentences.zh: 之傑密請移鹿卿浙東提點刑獄，加直秘閣兼提舉常平。

translations.literal: Zhijie secretly requested that Luqing be moved to judicial intendant of Zhedong, with promotion to Direct Secretariat Drafter and concurrent Ever-Normal Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Zhijie secretly sought to transfer Luqing to Zhedong judicial intendant, with promotion to Direct Secretariat Drafter and concurrent Ever-Normal Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 鹿卿言罷浮鹽經界鹼地，先撤相家所築，就捕者自言：「我相府人。

translations.literal: Luqing spoke for abolishing floating salt and delimiting alkaline lands; he first tore down a dike built by a chief minister's family, and the arrested man said of himself, "I am a man of the chief minister's mansion."
translations.idiomatic: Luqing urged abolishing floating salt levies and fixing alkaline land boundaries. He first demolished a dike built by a chief minister's kin. The man arrested said, "I serve the chief minister's household."

sentences.zh: 」鹿卿曰：「行法必自貴近始。

translations.literal: Luqing said, "In enforcing the law one must begin with the honored and near."
translations.idiomatic: Luqing replied, "Law must begin with those nearest power."

sentences.zh: 」卒論如法。

translations.literal: In the end he was prosecuted according to law.
translations.idiomatic: In the end the offender was punished according to law.

sentences.zh: 丞相史彌遠之弟通判溫州。

translations.literal: The chief minister Shi Miyuan's younger brother served as vice prefect of Wenzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Chief Minister Shi Miyuan's younger brother served as vice prefect of Wenzhou.

sentences.zh: 利韓世忠家寶玩，籍之，鹿卿奏削其官。

translations.literal: Coveting the treasures of Han Shizhong's household, he registered them for seizure; Luqing memorialized that his office be struck from the rolls.
translations.idiomatic: He coveted the treasures of Han Shizhong's household and had them registered for confiscation. Luqing memorialized to strip him of office.

sentences.zh: 初，鹿卿檄衢州推官馮惟說決婺獄，惟說素廉平，至則辨曲直，出淹禁。

translations.literal: Earlier Luqing had ordered the Quzhou investigating officer Feng Weishuo to decide a Wu case; Weishuo had always been incorrupt and fair, and on arrival distinguished right from wrong and released those long imprisoned.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Luqing had assigned Quzhou investigating officer Feng Weishuo to try a case in Wu. Weishuo, known for integrity, sorted right from wrong on arrival and freed long-imprisoned defendants.

sentences.zh: 大家不快其爲，會鄉人居言路，乃屬劾惟說。

translations.literal: Great families were displeased with his conduct; it happened that a fellow townsman held a remonstrance post, and he was set to impeach Weishuo.
translations.idiomatic: Powerful families resented his work. A fellow townsman then held a remonstrance post and arranged to impeach Weishuo.

sentences.zh: 州索印紙，惟說笑曰：「是猶可以仕乎？

translations.literal: The prefecture demanded his credential paper; Weishuo smiled and said, "Can one still serve in such circumstances?"
translations.idiomatic: The prefecture demanded his official seal. Weishuo smiled and said, "Can one still serve under such conditions?"

sentences.zh: 」自題詩印紙而去。

translations.literal: He inscribed a poem on the credential paper himself and departed.
translations.idiomatic: He inscribed a poem on the seal document and left.

sentences.zh: 衢州鄭逢辰以繆舉，鹿卿以委使不當，相繼自劾，且共和其詩。

translations.literal: Zheng Fengchen of Quzhou had been promoted by error; Luqing, because the commission of duty was improper, successively impeached himself, and together they composed poems in shared verse.
translations.idiomatic: Quzhou's Zheng Fengchen had been promoted by mistake. Luqing, holding the appointment improper, repeatedly impeached himself and joined Fengchen in exchanging poems.

sentences.zh: 御史兼二人劾罷之。

translations.literal: The censor jointly impeached both and had them dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: A censor impeached both and secured their dismissal.

sentences.zh: 及知泉州，改贛州，皆辭。

translations.literal: When he was appointed to Quanzhou and then transferred to Ganzhou, he declined both.
translations.idiomatic: Offered Quanzhou and then Ganzhou, he declined both.

sentences.zh: 遷浙西提點刑獄、江淮都大坑冶，皆以病固辭，遂主管玉局觀。

translations.literal: Promoted to judicial intendant of Zhexi and Grand Commissioner of Mining in the Jiang-Huai region, he firmly declined each on grounds of illness and was finally made director of the Jade Bureau Observatory.
translations.idiomatic: Named Zhexi judicial intendant and Grand Commissioner of Jiang-Huai mining, he refused both posts citing illness and was finally made director of the Jade Bureau Observatory.

sentences.zh: 及召還，又辭，改直寶章閣知甯國府，提舉江東常平，又辭。

translations.literal: When summoned back he declined again; he was changed to Direct Drafter of the Baozhang Hall and prefect of Ningguo, with charge of Jiangdong Ever-Normal affairs, and again declined.
translations.idiomatic: When recalled he declined again. He was offered Direct Drafter of the Baozhang Hall and the Ningguo prefecture with Jiangdong Ever-Normal duties, and declined once more.

sentences.zh: 淳祐三年，以右司召，猶辭。

translations.literal: In the third year of Chunyou he was summoned to the Right Office and still declined.
translations.idiomatic: In Chunyou year 3 he was summoned to the Right Office and still refused.

sentences.zh: 丞相杜范遺書曰：「直道不容，使人擊節。

translations.literal: Chief Minister Du Fan sent a letter saying, "The upright way finds no room— it makes one beat the table in admiration."
translations.idiomatic: Chief Minister Du Fan wrote: "The upright path has no place at court—it makes one strike the table in admiration."

sentences.zh: 君不出，豈以馮惟說故耶？

translations.literal: Will you not come forth? Is it because of Feng Weishuo?
translations.idiomatic: Will you not emerge? Is it because of Feng Weishuo?

sentences.zh: 惟說行將有命矣。

translations.literal: Weishuo will soon receive an appointment.
translations.idiomatic: Weishuo will soon receive an appointment.

sentences.zh: 」鹿卿乃出。

translations.literal: Only then did Luqing come forth.
translations.idiomatic: Only then did Luqing accept office.

sentences.zh: 擢太府少卿兼右司。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Vice Minister of the Court of the Imperial Treasury with concurrent service in the Right Office.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Vice Minister of the Imperial Treasury with concurrent duty in the Right Office.

sentences.zh: 入對，請定國本、正紀綱、立規模，「時事多艱，人心易搖，無獨力任重之臣，無守節伏義之士，願蚤決大計」。

translations.literal: Appearing before the throne, he requested fixing the imperial succession, rectifying discipline and statutes, and establishing a framework, saying: "Affairs of the time are mostly arduous and men's hearts easily swayed; there are no ministers who alone bear heavy responsibility, no gentlemen who guard their integrity and lay down their lives for principle— I pray that the great decision be made early."
translations.idiomatic: At court he urged fixing the imperial succession, restoring discipline, and setting a governing framework: "The times are hard and hearts are easily shaken. There is no minister who bears the full weight alone, no gentleman who dies for principle. I beg that the great decision be made soon."

sentences.zh: 上嘉納之。

translations.literal: The emperor praised and accepted it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised and accepted his counsel.

sentences.zh: 兼中書門下省檢正諸房公事，兼崇政殿說書。

translations.literal: He was concurrently made rectifier of the various offices of the Secretariat-Chancellery and lecturer at the Chongzheng Hall.
translations.idiomatic: He was concurrently made rectifier of Secretariat-Chancellery offices and lecturer at the Chongzheng Hall.

sentences.zh: 逾年，兼權吏部侍郎。

translations.literal: After more than a year he was concurrently made acting Vice Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: After a year he was made acting Vice Minister of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 時議使執政分治兵財，鹿卿執議不可。

translations.literal: At the time it was proposed that the chief ministers divide military and fiscal affairs; Luqing held that this could not be done.
translations.idiomatic: Some proposed splitting military and fiscal authority between chief ministers. Luqing insisted it could not be done.

sentences.zh: 以疾丐祠，遷右文殿修撰、知平江府兼發運副使。

translations.literal: On grounds of illness he begged a temple post and was moved to Right Culture Hall Compiler and prefect of Pingjiang with concurrent duty as transport vice commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Citing illness, he sought a temple post and was transferred to Right Culture Hall Compiler, prefect of Pingjiang, and transport vice commissioner.

sentences.zh: 力丐祠，上諭丞相挽留之。

translations.literal: He earnestly begged a temple post; the emperor instructed the chief minister to detain him.
translations.idiomatic: He earnestly sought retirement again. The emperor told the chief minister to keep him at court.

sentences.zh: 召權兵部侍郎，固辭，上令丞相以書招之，鹿卿至，又極言君子小人，切於當世之務。

translations.literal: He was summoned as acting Vice Minister of War; he firmly declined, and the emperor ordered the chief minister to summon him by letter; when Luqing arrived he again spoke to the utmost on gentlemen and petty men, pressing on the urgent affairs of the age.
translations.idiomatic: Summoned as acting Vice Minister of War, he refused until the emperor ordered the chief minister to write him in. When he came he again spoke bluntly on gentlemen and petty men and the urgent needs of the age.

sentences.zh: 兼國子祭酒，權禮部侍郎，兼同修國史，兼實錄院同修撰，兼侍講，兼權給事中。

translations.literal: He was concurrently Chancellor of the Directorate of Education, acting Vice Minister of Rites, concurrent compiler of the National History, concurrent compiler of the Veritable Records, concurrent lecturer, and acting Controller of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He concurrently served as Chancellor of the Directorate of Education, acting Vice Minister of Rites, National History compiler, Veritable Records compiler, imperial lecturer, and acting Controller of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 鹿卿言「瑣闥之職無所不當問，比年命下而給捨不得知，請復舊制」。

translations.literal: Luqing said, "The duty of the remonstrance office has no matter it should not question; in recent years when orders were issued the drafting and review officers did not know of them— I request restoration of the former system."
translations.idiomatic: Luqing said, "The remonstrance office should question every matter. In recent years edicts have been issued without the drafters' knowledge. I ask that the old system be restored."

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: The emperor followed this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 上眷遇冞篤而忌者浸多，有撰偽疏托鹿卿以傳播，曆詆宰相至百執事，鹿卿初不知也，遂力辨上前，因乞去，上曰：「去，則中奸人之計矣。

translations.literal: The emperor's favor grew ever deeper while those who resented him gradually increased; someone forged a memorial in Luqing's name and circulated it, slandering the chief minister down to the hundred officials; Luqing at first did not know of it, then forcefully explained himself before the throne and therefore begged to leave; the emperor said, "If you go, you will fall into the schemers' plot."
translations.idiomatic: Imperial favor deepened, but enemies multiplied. Someone forged a memorial in Luqing's name and circulated it, attacking the chief minister and the entire bureaucracy. Unaware at first, Luqing then defended himself before the throne and begged to resign. The emperor said, "If you leave, you will play into the plotters' hands."

sentences.zh: 」令臨安府根捕，事連勢要，獄不及竟。

translations.literal: He ordered the Lin'an prefecture to trace and arrest the culprits; the case touched powerful interests, and the prosecution could not be brought to completion.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered Lin'an authorities to investigate, but the case touched powerful interests and never reached a conclusion.

sentences.zh: 遷禮部侍郎。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Vice Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Vice Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 累疏告老，授寶章閣待制、知甯國府，而引年之疏五上，不允，提舉鴻禧觀，遂致仕，進華文閣待制。

translations.literal: He repeatedly memorialized to announce old age; he was granted Baozhang Hall Gentleman and prefect of Ningguo, yet five memorials citing his years went up without acceptance; he was put in charge of the Hongxi Temple and then retired, and was advanced to Gentleman of the Huawen Hall.
translations.idiomatic: He repeatedly sought retirement and was granted Gentleman of the Baozhang Hall and the Ningguo prefecture, but five petitions citing his age went unanswered. He was placed over Hongxi Temple, then retired, and was advanced to Gentleman of the Huawen Hall.

sentences.zh: 卒，遺表聞，贈四官。

translations.literal: When he died his final memorial reached the throne; four ranks of office were posthumously granted.
translations.idiomatic: After his death his final memorial reached the throne, and four ranks of office were granted posthumously.

sentences.zh: 鹿卿居家孝友，喜怒不形，恩怨俱泯，宗族鄉黨，各得歡心。

translations.literal: At home Luqing was filial and friendly; he did not show anger or joy on his face, and both favor and injury were forgotten; within clan and village each found cause for gladness.
translations.idiomatic: At home he was filial and kind, never showing anger or joy on his face, forgetting both favors and injuries. Clan and neighbors alike found joy in him.

sentences.zh: 居官廉約清峻，豪發不妄取，一廬僅庇風雨。

translations.literal: In office he was frugal, restrained, and pure and severe; he did not take a single hair wrongly, and one cottage barely sheltered him from wind and rain.
translations.idiomatic: In office he was frugal and austere, never taking so much as a hair unjustly. A single cottage barely kept out wind and rain.

sentences.zh: 所著有《泉谷文集》、奏議、講義、《鹽楮議政稿》、《曆官對越集》，手編《漢唐文類》、《文苑菁華》，諡清正。

translations.literal: Among his writings were the Spring Valley Collection, memorials, lecture notes, Salt and Paper Currency Policy Drafts, Audience Memorials from His Offices, and his own compilation of Han and Tang literary categories and the Forest of Letters; his posthumous title was Upright and Pure.
translations.idiomatic: His works included the Spring Valley Collection, memorials, lecture notes, Salt and Paper Currency Policy Drafts, Audience Memorials from His Offices, and his own compilations of Han-Tang literature and the Forest of Letters. His posthumous title was Upright and Pure.

sentences.zh: 趙逢龍

translations.literal: Zhao Fenglong
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Fenglong

sentences.zh: 趙逢龍，字應甫，慶元之鄞人。

translations.literal: Zhao Fenglong, styled Yingfu, was a man of Yin in Qingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Fenglong, courtesy name Yingfu, was from Yin in Qingyuan circuit.

sentences.zh: 刻苦自修，爲學淹博純實。

translations.literal: Through bitter self-cultivation he made his learning broad, deep, and pure.
translations.idiomatic: Through rigorous self-cultivation he achieved learning that was broad, deep, and solid.

sentences.zh: 登嘉定十六年進士第。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination in the sixteenth year of Jiading.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in Jiading year 16.

sentences.zh: 授國子正、太學博士，曆知興國、信、衢、衡、袁五州，提舉廣東、湖南、福建常平。

translations.literal: He was appointed Rectifier of the Directorate, Erudite of the Imperial Academy, and in succession served as prefect of Xingguo, Xin, Qu, Heng, and Yuan, and as Ever-Normal Commissioner in Guangdong, Hunan, and Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Rectifier of the Directorate and Erudite of the Imperial Academy, then successively as prefect of Xingguo, Xin, Qu, Heng, and Yuan, and as Ever-Normal Commissioner in Guangdong, Hunan, and Fujian.

sentences.zh: 每至官，有司例設供張，悉命撤去，日具蔬飯，坐公署，事至即面問決遣。

translations.literal: Whenever he reached a post, the local offices by custom set out reception furnishings; he ordered them all removed, took only plain vegetable meals each day, and sat in the public hall; when business arrived he questioned the parties face to face and decided on the spot.
translations.idiomatic: At every post local offices customarily prepared lavish reception quarters. He had them all dismantled, ate simple vegetable meals daily, and sat in the public hall, deciding cases face to face as they arose.

sentences.zh: 爲政務寬恕，撫諭惻怛，一以天理民彝爲言，民是以不忍欺。

translations.literal: In governing he strove for leniency, comforting and instructing with heartfelt compassion, always speaking in terms of heavenly principle and human moral nature, so that the people for this reason could not bear to deceive him.
translations.idiomatic: He governed with leniency, comforting people with sincere compassion and appealing always to heavenly principle and human moral nature, so that the people could not bring themselves to deceive him.

sentences.zh: 居官自常奉外，一介不取。

translations.literal: In office, apart from his regular salary, he took not even one cash.
translations.idiomatic: Beyond his regular salary he accepted not a single coin in office.

sentences.zh: 民賦有逋負，悉爲代輸。

translations.literal: When the people owed taxes in arrears, he paid them all on their behalf.
translations.idiomatic: When taxpayers fell into arrears, he paid their debts himself.

sentences.zh: 尤究心荒政，以羨余爲平糴本。

translations.literal: He devoted himself especially to famine policy, using surpluses as capital for stabilizing grain sales.
translations.idiomatic: He devoted special attention to famine relief, using budget surpluses to fund grain stabilization.

sentences.zh: 遷將作監，拜宗正少卿兼侍講。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Director of Palace Construction and appointed Vice Minister of the Imperial Clan with concurrent duty as lecturer.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Director of Palace Construction and appointed Vice Minister of the Imperial Clan with concurrent duty as imperial lecturer.

sentences.zh: 凡道德性命之蘊，禮樂刑政之事，縷縷爲上開陳。

translations.literal: Whether the store of moral nature and fate, or matters of rites, music, punishments, and government, he laid them out thread by thread before the throne.
translations.idiomatic: Whether on moral nature and destiny, or on rites, music, punishments, and government, he unfolded each topic in careful detail before the throne.

sentences.zh: 疏奏甚衆，稿悉焚棄。

translations.literal: His memorials were very numerous; the drafts he burned entirely.
translations.idiomatic: He submitted many memorials, but burned every draft.

sentences.zh: 年八十有八終於家。

translations.literal: At eighty-eight years he died at home.
translations.idiomatic: He died at home at the age of eighty-eight.

sentences.zh: 逢龍家居講道，四方從遊者皆爲钜公名士。

translations.literal: At home Fenglong lectured on the Way; those who came from the four directions to study with him were all great lords and eminent scholars.
translations.idiomatic: At home he lectured on the Way, and scholars who came from every direction to study with him were great ministers and eminent scholars.

sentences.zh: 丞相葉夢鼎出判慶元，修弟子禮，常謂師門庳陋，欲市其鄰居充拓之。

translations.literal: Chief Minister Ye Mengding, when leaving office to serve in Qingyuan, observed the disciple's rites toward him and often said the master's gate was low and cramped and wished to buy the neighboring houses to expand it.
translations.idiomatic: Chief Minister Ye Mengding, on leaving office to serve in Qingyuan, treated him as a teacher and often said the master's gate was too cramped, wishing to buy neighboring houses to enlarge it.

sentences.zh: 逢龍曰：「鄰里粗安，一旦驚擾，彼雖勉從，我能無愧於心！

translations.literal: Fenglong said, "The neighborhood is roughly at peace; if suddenly disturbed, though they might yield reluctantly, could I be without shame in my heart?"
translations.idiomatic: Fenglong said, "The neighborhood is at peace. If we suddenly disturb it, neighbors may yield reluctantly—but could I face them without shame?"

sentences.zh: 」逢龍寡嗜欲，不好名，揚曆日久，泊然不知富貴之味。

translations.literal: Fenglong had few desires and did not love fame; though he rose through offices over many years, he remained indifferent and did not know the taste of wealth and honor.
translations.idiomatic: Fenglong had few desires and cared little for fame. Though he served in office for many years, he remained indifferent to wealth and rank.

sentences.zh: 或問何以裕後，逢龍笑曰：「吾憂子孫學行不進，不患其饑寒也。」

translations.literal: Someone asked how to provide for posterity; Fenglong smiled and said, "I worry that my sons and grandsons' learning and conduct will not advance—I do not worry that they will suffer cold or hunger."
translations.idiomatic: Asked how to provide for posterity, he smiled and said, "I worry that my descendants' learning and conduct will not advance. I do not worry that they will go hungry or cold."

sentences.zh: 趙汝騰

translations.literal: Zhao Ruteng
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Ruteng

sentences.zh: 趙汝騰，字茂實，宗室子也。

translations.literal: Zhao Ruteng, styled Maoshi, was a member of the imperial clan.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Ruteng, courtesy name Maoshi, was a member of the imperial clan.

sentences.zh: 居福州。

translations.literal: He dwelt in Fuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He made his home in Fuzhou.

sentences.zh: 寶慶二年進士。

translations.literal: Jinshi in the second year of Baoqing.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in the second year of the Baoqing era (1226).

sentences.zh: 曆官差主管禮、兵部架閣，遷籍田令，召試館職，授秘書省正字，升校書郎，尋升秘書郎兼史館校勘。

translations.literal: Through successive offices he was assigned to supervise the archive shelves of the Ministries of Rites and War, became Director of the Sacrificial Field, was summoned for a trial appointment in the Hanlin Academy service, was granted Secretary Rectifier, was promoted to Collator, and soon after was promoted to Secretary Gentleman while also serving as collator in the Historiography Office.
translations.idiomatic: In his official career he successively supervised the archival shelves of the Ministries of Rites and War, served as Director of the Sacrificial Field, was called for a probationary Hanlin post, and was appointed Secretary Rectifier, then Collator, and soon Secretary Gentleman with concurrent duty as historiography collator.

sentences.zh: 輪對，言節用先自乘輿宮掖始。

translations.literal: At a rotating audience he spoke, saying that economy must begin with the imperial carriage and the inner palace.
translations.idiomatic: In a palace audience he urged that frugality must begin with the emperor's own conveyances and the inner palace.

sentences.zh: 兼玉牒所檢討官，以直煥章閣知溫州，進直徽猷閣、江東提點刑獄，又進直寶文閣，差知婺州。

translations.literal: Concurrently he was an examining officer of the Imperial Genealogy Office; with direct appointment to the Huazhang Hall he became prefect of Wenzhou; he advanced to direct appointment to the Huiyou Hall and Jiangdong judicial intendant; he advanced again to direct appointment to the Baowen Hall and was assigned as prefect of Wuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He also served as examiner in the Imperial Genealogy Office, then with a direct Huazhang Hall appointment became prefect of Wenzhou; he rose to a direct Huiyou Hall post as Jiangdong judicial intendant, and again to a direct Baowen Hall appointment as prefect of Wuzhou.

sentences.zh: 召赴闕，遷起居舍人，兼權中書舍人，升起居郎，時暫兼權吏部侍郎，兼國史編修、實錄檢討，兼同修國史、實錄院同修撰，兼侍講，遷吏部侍郎兼侍講，權工部尚書兼權中書舍人，皆兼同修撰，以左司諫陳垓論罷。

translations.literal: Summoned to court, he was moved to Gentleman Attendant of the Bedchamber, concurrently acting as Drafting Academician of the Secretariat, then promoted to Attendant Gentleman; for a time he concurrently acted as Vice Minister of Personnel, and concurrently edited the national history, examined the veritable records, and jointly compiled the national history and veritable records in the Historiography Office, and concurrently lectured; he was moved to Vice Minister of Personnel with concurrent lecturing, acting concurrently as Minister of Works and acting Drafting Academician, all with concurrent joint compilation—all dismissed on the memorial of Left Department Remonstrator Chen Kai.
translations.idiomatic: Recalled to court, he became Gentleman Attendant of the Bedchamber and acting Drafting Academician, then Attendant Gentleman; for a time he also acted as Vice Minister of Personnel while editing the national history, examining the veritable records, and serving as joint compiler in the Historiography Office and as lecturer; he rose to Vice Minister of Personnel with concurrent lecturing, then acting Minister of Works and acting Drafting Academician, always with joint compilation duties—until Left Remonstrator Chen Kai's memorial brought his dismissal.

sentences.zh: 召爲禮部尚書兼給事中，兼修國史、實錄院修撰。

translations.literal: He was summoned as Minister of Rites with concurrent Reviewer, and concurrent compiler in the Historiography Office and Veritable Records Office.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled as Minister of Rites and Reviewer, with concurrent duties in the Historiography and Veritable Records offices.

sentences.zh: 入奏，言：「前後奸諛之臣，傷善害賢，自取穹官要職，何益于陛下，而深損於聖德。

translations.literal: Entering to memorialize, he said: 'Successive treacherous and fawning ministers have harmed the good and injured the worthy, themselves taking lofty offices and key posts—what benefit to Your Majesty, yet how deep the injury to sagely virtue.'
translations.idiomatic: In audience he said: 'Time and again treacherous flatterers have harmed the worthy and injured the good, yet seized the highest offices and key posts—what good does that do Your Majesty, while it deeply wounds your sagely virtue?'

sentences.zh: 興利之臣，移東就西，順適宮禁，自遂溪壑無厭之欲，何益于陛下，而深戕于國脈。

translations.literal: Ministers who seek profit shift goods from east to west to suit the inner palace, themselves satisfying bottomless greed—what benefit to Your Majesty, yet how deep the wound to the nation's vital pulse.'
translations.idiomatic: 'Those who chase profit shift resources this way and that to please the inner palace, filling their own bottomless greed—what good does that do Your Majesty, while it deeply cuts the nation's lifeblood?'

sentences.zh: 則陛下私惠群小之心，可以息矣。

translations.literal: Then the heart of Your Majesty to show private favor to the multitude of petty men can be stilled.'
translations.idiomatic: 'In that case Your Majesty's inclination to show private favor to petty men can at last be laid to rest.'

sentences.zh: 」又言：「陛下有用君子之名，無用君子之實。」

translations.literal: He also said: 'Your Majesty has the name of employing gentlemen, but not the reality of employing gentlemen.'
translations.idiomatic: He also said: 'Your Majesty has the reputation of employing true gentlemen, but not the reality.'

sentences.zh: 兼直學士院，拜翰林學士兼知制誥，兼侍讀。

translations.literal: Concurrently in the Academy of Scholars, he was appointed Hanlin Academician with concurrent drafting of edicts, and concurrent Reader-in-Waiting.
translations.idiomatic: With concurrent duty in the Academy of Scholars, he was made Hanlin Academician and drafter of edicts, and Reader-in-Waiting.

sentences.zh: 辭歸故里，累召，力辭，以龍圖閣學士知紹興府、浙東安撫使。

translations.literal: He declined and returned to his native place; repeatedly summoned, he firmly declined, and with Dragon Diagram Hall academician's rank became prefect of Shaoxing and Eastern Zhejiang pacification commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He resigned and went home; though summoned again and again he firmly refused, and was finally made Dragon Diagram Hall academician, prefect of Shaoxing, and Eastern Zhejiang pacification commissioner.

sentences.zh: 召至闕，以端明殿學士提舉佑神觀，兼翰林學士承旨，知泉州、知州南外宗正事，復提舉佑神觀兼侍讀。

translations.literal: Summoned to court, with Duanming Hall academician's rank he was made director of the Youshen Abbey, concurrently Chief Hanlin Academician, prefect of Quanzhou, and director of the Southern Outer Imperial Clan Bureau; again he was made director of the Youshen Abbey with concurrent Reader-in-Waiting.
translations.idiomatic: Called to court as Duanming Hall academician, he directed the Youshen Abbey while serving as Chief Hanlin Academician, prefect of Quanzhou, and director of the Southern Outer Imperial Clan Bureau; later he again directed the Youshen Abbey with concurrent Reader-in-Waiting.

sentences.zh: 兼翰林學士承旨。

translations.literal: Concurrently Chief Hanlin Academician.
translations.idiomatic: He also served as Chief Hanlin Academician.

sentences.zh: 景定二年，卒，遺表上，特贈四官。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jingding he died; his final memorial was submitted, and he was specially posthumously promoted four ranks.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Jingding (1261) he died; when his final memorial reached the throne he was specially posthumously promoted four ranks.

sentences.zh: 孫夢觀

translations.literal: Sun Mengguan
translations.idiomatic: Sun Mengguan

sentences.zh: 孫夢觀，字守叔，慶元府慈溪人。

translations.literal: Sun Mengguan, style name Shoushu, was a man of Cixi in Qingyuan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Mengguan, courtesy name Shoushu, was from Cixi in Qingyuan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 寶慶二年進士。

translations.literal: Jinshi in the second year of Baoqing.
translations.idiomatic: He received the jinshi degree in the second year of Baoqing (1226).

sentences.zh: 調桂陽軍教授、浙西提舉司幹辦公事，差主管吏部架閣文字，爲武學諭。

translations.literal: He was posted as professor at Guiyang Commandery, clerk in the Western Zhejiang Commissariat, assigned to supervise the archive documents of the Ministry of Personnel, and made Erudite of the Military School.
translations.idiomatic: He served as professor at Guiyang Commandery, clerk in the Western Zhejiang transport office, supervisor of Personnel Ministry archive documents, and Erudite of the Military School.

sentences.zh: 輪對，言：「人主不容有所憚，尤不容有所玩，憚則有言而不能容，玩則雖容其言而不能用。

translations.literal: At a rotating audience he said: 'The sovereign must not permit anything to be feared, and above all must not permit anything to be trifled with; if there is fear, then there are words that cannot be received, and if there is trifling, then though words are received they cannot be used.'
translations.idiomatic: In a palace audience he said: 'A ruler must fear nothing in his counsellors—yet he must never treat their words lightly. Fear means counsel spoken but not heard; levity means counsel heard but never acted upon.'

sentences.zh: 」力請外，添差通判嚴州，主管崇道觀，召爲武學博士、太常寺丞兼諸王宮大小學教授，大宗正丞兼屯田郎官、將作少監。

translations.literal: He strongly requested an outside post, was given additional assignment as vice prefect of Yanzhou, directed the Chongdao Abbey, and was summoned as Erudite of the Military School, Vice Director of the Court of Sacrifices with concurrent instruction in the princes' great and small schools, Vice Director of the Imperial Clan Court with concurrent Grain Tax Bureau and Assistant Director of Palace Construction.
translations.idiomatic: He pressed for a provincial post, received an additional assignment as vice prefect of Yanzhou and director of the Chongdao Abbey, then was recalled as Military School erudite, Vice Director of Sacrifices with concurrent teaching in the imperial princes' schools, and Vice Director of the Imperial Clan Court with concurrent posts in the Grain Tax Bureau and Palace Construction.

sentences.zh: 知嘉興府，仍舊班兼右司郎官、將作監。

translations.literal: He became prefect of Jiaxing, retaining his former rank while concurrently Right Department Bureau officer and Director of Palace Construction.
translations.idiomatic: As prefect of Jiaxing he kept his former rank while also serving in the Right Department and as Director of Palace Construction.

sentences.zh: 轉對，極言：「風憲之地，未聞有十八疏攻一竦者。

translations.literal: At a further audience he spoke forcefully: 'In the place of moral oversight, one has never heard of eighteen memorials attacking one man.'
translations.idiomatic: In another audience he said bluntly: 'At the censorial court one never hears of eighteen memorials aimed at a single man.'

sentences.zh: 封駁之司，未聞有三舍人不肯草制者。

translations.literal: In the office of seal-and-reject, one has never heard of three drafting academicians refusing to draft an edict.'
translations.idiomatic: At the seal-and-reject office one never hears of three drafting academicians refusing to draft an edict.'

sentences.zh: 道揆不明，法守滋亂，天下之權將有所寄，而倒持之患作。

translations.literal: The moral compass is unclear, law and order grow more chaotic, the empire's power will find somewhere to lodge, and the calamity of holding the hilt while the blade points inward arises.'
translations.idiomatic: The moral compass is clouded and the laws in disarray; power in the realm is being handed to others, and the disaster of holding the sword by the blade is upon us.'

sentences.zh: 」當路者滋不悅。

translations.literal: Those in power grew still more displeased.
translations.idiomatic: Those in power were only more displeased.

sentences.zh: 出知泉州兼提舉市舶，改知甯國府。

translations.literal: Those in power grew still more displeased.
translations.idiomatic: Those in power were only more displeased.

sentences.zh: 蠲逋減賦，無算泛入者盡籍於公帑。

translations.literal: He went out as prefect of Quanzhou with concurrent maritime trade intendant, and was changed to prefect of Ningguo.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out as prefect of Quanzhou with concurrent maritime trade intendant, then transferred to Ningguo.

sentences.zh: 戶部遣官督賦，急若星火，闔郡皇駭，莫知爲計。

translations.literal: He remitted arrears and reduced levies; all miscellaneous irregular receipts were fully registered in the public treasury.
translations.idiomatic: He cancelled tax arrears and cut levies, and every irregular levy was entered into the public treasury.

sentences.zh: 夢觀曰：「吾寧委官以去，毋寧病民以留。

translations.literal: The Ministry of Revenue sent officials to press collection; urgent as sparks, the whole prefecture was terrified and knew not what to do.
translations.idiomatic: When Revenue officials came to press collection with fire-breath urgency, the whole prefecture was panic-stricken and at a loss.

sentences.zh: 」力丐祠，且將以府印牒所遣官，所遣官聞之夜遁。

translations.literal: Mengguan said: 'I would rather surrender my office and leave than harm the people and remain.'
translations.idiomatic: Mengguan said: 'I would rather give up my post than stay on and harm the people.'

sentences.zh: 他日夢觀去甯國，人言之爲之流涕。

translations.literal: He pressed strongly for a temple post, and was about to use the prefectural seal to serve notice on the dispatched officials; hearing this, the dispatched officials fled by night.
translations.idiomatic: He begged hard for a temple appointment and was about to serve the Revenue agents with the prefectural seal; when they heard of it they fled overnight.

sentences.zh: 丞相董槐召還，帝問江東廉吏，槐首以夢觀對，帝說，乃遷司農少卿兼資善堂贊讀。

translations.literal: Another day when Mengguan left Ningguo, the people spoke of him with tears.
translations.idiomatic: When he later left Ningguo, the people spoke of him with tears in their eyes.

sentences.zh: 輪對，謂：「今內外之臣，恃陛下以各遂其私，而陛下獨一無可恃，可爲寒心！

translations.literal: Chief Councillor Dong Huai summoned him back; the Emperor asked about incorrupt officials in Jiangdong, and Huai named Mengguan first; the Emperor was pleased and moved him to Vice Minister of Revenue with concurrent Reader in the Zishan Hall.
translations.idiomatic: Chief Councillor Dong Huai had him recalled; when the emperor asked for honest officials in Jiangdong, Huai named Mengguan first. Pleased, the emperor made him Vice Minister of Revenue and reader in the Zishan Hall.

sentences.zh: 」次論：「郡國當爲斯民計，朝廷當爲郡國計。

translations.literal: At a rotating audience he said: 'Now inside and outside, ministers rely on Your Majesty so each may pursue his private ends, while Your Majesty alone has nothing to rely on—how chilling!'
translations.idiomatic: In audience he said: 'Ministers inside and outside the court now rely on Your Majesty only so each may pursue his private ends, while Your Majesty alone has nothing to rely on—how chilling a thought!'

sentences.zh: 乞命大臣應自前主計之臣奪州縣之利而歸版曹者，復歸所屬，庶幾郡國蒙一分之寬，則斯民亦受一分之賜。

translations.literal: Next he argued: 'Prefectures and commanderies should plan for these people; the court should plan for the prefectures and commanderies.'
translations.idiomatic: He went on: 'Prefectures should plan for the people; the court should plan for the prefectures.'

sentences.zh: 」帝善其言。

translations.literal: The Emperor approved his words.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved his words.

sentences.zh: 遷太府卿、宗正少卿，兼給事中、起居舍人、起居郎。

translations.literal: He was moved to Minister of the Imperial Treasury, Vice Director of the Imperial Clan Court, concurrently Reviewer, Gentleman Attendant of the Bedchamber, and Attendant Gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Minister of the Imperial Treasury and Vice Director of the Imperial Clan Court, with concurrent posts as Reviewer, Gentleman Attendant, and Attendant Gentleman.

sentences.zh: 八上章辭免，以監察御史吳燧論罷，直龍圖閣與祠，授秘閣修撰、江淮等路提點鑄錢司公事。

translations.literal: Eight times he submitted memorials declining removal; he was dismissed on the memorial of Supervising Censor Wu Sui, given Dragon Diagram Hall academician with temple appointment, and granted Secretariat Compiler with charge of the Huai-Jiang and other circuits coinage office.
translations.idiomatic: Eight times he memorialized to decline further promotion; Supervising Censor Wu Sui's attack brought his dismissal, a Dragon Diagram Hall academician's temple post, and appointment as Secretariat compiler in charge of coinage for the Huai-Jiang circuit and others.

sentences.zh: 甫至官，即復召爲起居郎兼侍右侍郎、給事中兼贊讀，兼國子祭酒，權吏部侍郎。

translations.literal: Hardly had he reached his post when he was again summoned as Attendant Gentleman with concurrent Vice Minister of the Right Secretariat, Reviewer with concurrent Reader, and Chancellor of the National University, acting Vice Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He had barely taken up that post when he was recalled as Attendant Gentleman, acting Vice Minister of the Right Secretariat, Reviewer and reader, Chancellor of the National University, and acting Vice Minister of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 奏事抗論益切，以寵賂彰、仁賢逝、貨財偏聚爲言，且謂「未易相之前，敝政固不少；

translations.literal: Memorializing on affairs he argued ever more bluntly, speaking of favoritism displayed, worthies departed, and wealth unevenly gathered, and saying: 'Before the minister was easily changed, bad government was already plentiful;
translations.idiomatic: In memorials he argued ever more bluntly, denouncing displayed favoritism, departed worthies, and wealth piled in the wrong hands, and saying: 'Before the chief minister was replaced, abuses were already many;

sentences.zh: 既易相之後，敝政亦自若。

translations.literal: after the minister was easily changed, bad government remained as before.'
translations.idiomatic: after he was replaced, the abuses were just as they had been.'

sentences.zh: 」在廷之士皆危之。

translations.literal: Gentlemen at court were all endangered.
translations.idiomatic: Court officials all felt themselves in peril.

sentences.zh: 夢觀曰：「吾以一布衣蒙上恩至此，雖捐軀無以報，利鈍非所計也。」

translations.literal: Mengguan said: 'I, a plain scholar, have received such grace from above that though I give my body I cannot repay; gain or loss is not what I reckon.'
translations.idiomatic: Mengguan said: 'I began as a plain scholar and have received such grace from the throne that I could not repay it even with my life; I do not reckon gain or loss.'

sentences.zh: 力求補外，以集英殿修撰知建寧府。

translations.literal: He pressed to fill an outside post, and with Hall of Assembled Excellence compiler's rank became prefect of Jianning.
translations.idiomatic: He pressed for an outside appointment and, as compiler of the Hall of Assembled Excellence, became prefect of Jianning.

sentences.zh: 蠲租稅，省刑罰，郡人徐清叟、蔡抗以爲有古循吏風。

translations.literal: He remitted rent and taxes and reduced punishments; the people Xu Qingsou and Cai Kang regarded him as having the air of the ancient model officials.
translations.idiomatic: He cut rents and lightened punishments; the locals Xu Qingsou and Cai Kang said he had the manner of the old model magistrates.

sentences.zh: 民有夢從者甚郡，迎祠山神，出視之則夢觀也。

translations.literal: There were people who dreamed that a very great throng welcomed the Cishan god, and going out to look saw it was Mengguan.
translations.idiomatic: Some dreamed a vast crowd welcoming the god of Cishan; when they went out to look, it was Mengguan.

sentences.zh: 俄而夢觀得疾，口授遺表，不忘規諫，遂卒。

translations.literal: Before long Mengguan fell ill, dictated a final memorial, never forgetting remonstrance, and died.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he fell ill, dictated a final memorial still full of remonstrance, and died.

sentences.zh: 帝悼惜久之，賻銀帛三百。

translations.literal: The Emperor mourned him long, and granted three hundred in silver and silk as funeral gifts.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor mourned him at length and granted three hundred units of silver and silk for his funeral.

sentences.zh: 夢觀退然若不勝衣，然義所當爲，奮往直前；

translations.literal: Mengguan in retreat seemed scarcely able to bear his clothes, yet where righteousness required action he advanced straight ahead;
translations.idiomatic: Mengguan in person seemed almost too slight for his robes, yet where duty called he went straight ahead;

sentences.zh: 其居敗屋數間，布衣蔬食，而重名節云。

translations.literal: he dwelt in a few ruined rooms, wore plain cloth and ate simple food, yet valued name and integrity.
translations.idiomatic: he lived in a few ruined rooms on plain food and coarse cloth, yet held name and integrity dear.

sentences.zh: 洪天錫

translations.literal: Hong Tianxi
translations.idiomatic: Hong Tianxi

sentences.zh: 洪天錫，字君疇，泉州晉江人。

translations.literal: Hong Tianxi, style name Junchou, was a man of Jinjiang in Quanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Hong Tianxi, courtesy name Junchou, was from Jinjiang in Quanzhou.

sentences.zh: 寶慶二年進士。

translations.literal: Jinshi in the second year of Baoqing.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in the second year of Baoqing (1226).

sentences.zh: 授廣州司法。

translations.literal: He was appointed Guangzhou judicial officer.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed judicial officer of Guangzhou.

sentences.zh: 長吏盛氣待僚屬，天錫糾正爲多。

translations.literal: The chief official treated subordinates with overbearing air; Tianxi corrected him on many points.
translations.idiomatic: The chief official bullied his staff; Tianxi corrected him repeatedly.

sentences.zh: 丁內艱，免喪，調潮州司理。

translations.literal: Upon inner mourning he left office; when mourning ended he was transferred as judicial officer of Chaozhou.
translations.idiomatic: After his father's death he left office; when mourning ended he became judicial officer of Chaozhou.

sentences.zh: 勢家奪民田，天賜言於守，還之。

translations.literal: Powerful families seized commoners' fields; Tianxi spoke to the prefect and had them returned.
translations.idiomatic: When powerful families seized commoners' land, Tianxi appealed to the prefect and had the land returned.

sentences.zh: 帥方大琮辟真州判官，留置幕府。

translations.literal: Marshal Fang Dacong recruited him as vice magistrate of Zhenzhou and kept him in his staff.
translations.idiomatic: Marshal Fang Dacong took him on as vice magistrate of Zhenzhou and kept him on his staff.

sentences.zh: 改秩知古田縣。

translations.literal: His rank was changed and he became magistrate of Gutian County.
translations.idiomatic: His rank was changed and he became magistrate of Gutian County.

sentences.zh: 行鄉飲酒禮。

translations.literal: He carried out the district drinking ceremony.
translations.idiomatic: He conducted the local drinking ceremony.

sentences.zh: 邑劇，牒訴猥多，天錫剖決無留難。

translations.literal: The county was difficult; petitions and suits were numerous and tangled; Tianxi decided them without delay.
translations.idiomatic: The county was a difficult post with a tangle of suits; Tianxi disposed of them without delay.

sentences.zh: 有倚王邸勢殺人者，誅之不少貸。

translations.literal: There was one who relied on a princely mansion's power to kill a man; he executed him without the least leniency.
translations.idiomatic: When a man who relied on a princely mansion's power committed murder, Tianxi executed him without mercy.

sentences.zh: 調通判建寧府。

translations.literal: He was transferred as vice prefect of Jianning Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to vice prefect of Jianning.

sentences.zh: 大水，擅發常平倉振之。

translations.literal: In great flood he on his own authority opened the Ever-Normal Granary to relieve the people.
translations.idiomatic: During a great flood he opened the Ever-Normal Granary on his own authority to relieve the people.

sentences.zh: 擢諸司糧料院，拜監察御史兼說書。

translations.literal: He was promoted to the various offices' Grain Provisioning Institute, and appointed Supervising Censor with concurrent Lecturer.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to the Grain Provisioning Institute and appointed Supervising Censor with concurrent Lecturer.

sentences.zh: 累疏言：「天下之患三：宦官也，外戚也，小人也。

translations.literal: In repeated memorials he said: 'The empire's calamities are three: eunuchs, maternal kin, and petty men.'
translations.idiomatic: In repeated memorials he said: 'The empire's three calamities are eunuchs, imperial in-laws, and petty men.'

sentences.zh: 」劾董宋臣、謝堂、厲文翁，理宗力護文翁，天錫又言：「不斥文翁，必爲王府累。

translations.literal: He impeached Dong Songchen, Xie Tang, and Li Weng; Emperor Lizong strongly shielded Weng, and Tianxi again said: 'If Weng is not expelled, he will surely become a burden to the imperial clan.'
translations.idiomatic: He impeached Dong Songchen, Xie Tang, and Li Weng; Emperor Lizong strongly shielded Weng, and Tianxi said again: 'Unless Weng is removed, he will surely become a burden to the imperial house.'

sentences.zh: 」上令吳燧宣諭再三，天錫力爭，謂：「貴幸作奸犯科，根柢蟠固，乃遲回護惜，不欲繩以法，勢焰愈張，紀綱愈壞，異時禍成，雖欲治之不可得矣。

translations.literal: The Emperor had Wu Sui announce the imperial will again and again; Tianxi argued forcefully, saying: 'When the honored and favored commit wickedness and violate law, their roots are deep and their hold firm—yet you hesitate and shield them, unwilling to bind them by law; their power only grows fiercer, discipline only breaks further, and when disaster comes later, even if you wish to correct it, it cannot be done.'
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had Wu Sui announce the imperial will again and again; Tianxi pressed his case, saying: 'When the favored commit crimes their roots run deep—yet the court hesitates and shields them rather than apply the law; their power only grows and discipline only rots, until when disaster comes it will be too late to mend.'

sentences.zh: 」上又出御劄，俾天錫易疏，欲自戒飭之。

translations.literal: The Emperor again issued an imperial note, wishing Tianxi to change his memorial so as to admonish himself.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor again sent a personal note, asking Tianxi to revise his memorial so the emperor might take it as self-admonition.

sentences.zh: 天錫又言：「自古奸人雖憑怙，其心未嘗不畏人主之知，苟知之而止於戒飭，則憑怙愈張，反不若未知之爲愈也。

translations.literal: Tianxi again said: 'Since ancient times wicked men, though they rely on favor, in their hearts have never failed to fear the sovereign's knowing; if knowing them yet stopping at self-admonition, then reliance grows fiercer—better not to have known them at all.'
translations.idiomatic: Tianxi replied: 'Since antiquity wicked men who enjoy favor still fear the ruler's knowledge; if the ruler knows them yet only admonishes himself, their hold grows only stronger—it would be better not to have known them at all.'

sentences.zh: 」章五上，出關待罪。

translations.literal: After five memorials he left the capital to await punishment.
translations.idiomatic: After five memorials he left the capital to await punishment.

sentences.zh: 詔二人已改命，宋臣續處之。

translations.literal: An edict said the two men had already been reassigned, and Songchen would continue to be dealt with.
translations.idiomatic: An edict said the two men had already been reassigned and that Songchen would continue to be dealt with.

sentences.zh: 天錫言：「臣留則宋臣去，宋臣留則臣當斥，願早賜裁斷。

translations.literal: Tianxi said: 'If I remain, Songchen goes; if Songchen remains, I should be expelled—may Your Majesty soon decide.'
translations.idiomatic: Tianxi said: 'If I stay, Songchen must go; if Songchen stays, I must be dismissed—let Your Majesty decide quickly.'

sentences.zh: 」越月，天雨土，天錫以其異爲蒙，力言陰陽君子小人之所以辨，又言修內司之爲民害者。

translations.literal: After a month, heaven rained earth; Tianxi took this prodigy as a veil, and spoke forcefully of how yin and yang distinguish the gentleman from the petty man, and again spoke of how the Inner Works Office harms the people.
translations.idiomatic: A month later earth fell from the sky; Tianxi took the omen as a cover and spoke forcefully on how yin and yang distinguish gentlemen from petty men, and again on how the Inner Works Office harms the people.

sentences.zh: 蜀中地震，浙、閩大水，又言：「上下窮空，遠近怨疾，獨貴戚巨閹享富貴耳。

translations.literal: Earthquake in Shu; great floods in Zhe and Min; he again said: 'Above and below are emptied, near and far are full of resentment—only the great favored and great eunuchs enjoy wealth and honor.'
translations.idiomatic: When Shu was shaken by earthquake and Zhe and Min by flood, he said again: 'Court and country are bankrupt, resentment runs everywhere—only the great favorites and great eunuchs still enjoy wealth and rank.'

sentences.zh: 舉天下窮且怨，陛下能獨與數十人者共天下乎？

translations.literal: When all under heaven are poor and resentful, can Your Majesty alone share the realm with a few dozen men?'
translations.idiomatic: 'When the whole realm is poor and resentful, can Your Majesty share the empire with only a few dozen men?'

sentences.zh: 」會吳民仲大論等列訴宋臣奪其田，天錫下其事有司，而御前提舉所移文謂田屬御莊，不當白台，儀鸞司亦牒常平。

translations.literal: When Wu commoners Zhong Dalun and others in series accused Songchen of seizing their fields, Tianxi referred the matter to the proper offices; yet the Imperial Advancement Office sent documents saying the fields belonged to the imperial estate and should not be reported to the censorate, and the Ceremonial Guard also sent documents to the Ever-Normal Office.
translations.idiomatic: When Wu commoners led by Zhong Dalun petitioned in succession that Songchen had seized their land, Tianxi referred the case to the proper offices; but the Imperial Advancement Office claimed the land as imperial estate and not to be reported to the censorate, and the Ceremonial Guard also sent papers to the Ever-Normal Office.

sentences.zh: 天錫謂：「御史所以雪冤，常平所以均役，若中貴人得以控之，則內外台可廢，猶爲國有紀綱乎？

translations.literal: Tianxi said: 'Censors exist to clear injustice; the Ever-Normal Office exists to equalize corvée—if inner favorites can control them, then inner and outer censorates may as well be abolished; is there still discipline in the state?'
translations.idiomatic: Tianxi said: 'Censors exist to right wrongs and the Ever-Normal Office to balance labor—if inner favorites can control them, the censorate might as well be abolished; does the state still have discipline?'

sentences.zh: 」乃申劾宋臣並盧允升而枚數其惡，上猶力護之。

translations.literal: He then submitted impeachment of Songchen together with Lu Yunsheng, itemizing their crimes; the Emperor still shielded them forcefully.
