translations.idiomatic: He then impeached Songchen together with Lu Yunsheng, itemizing their crimes; the emperor still shielded them.

sentences.zh: 天錫又言：「修內司供繕修而已，比年動曰'御前'，奸贓之老吏，跡捕之凶渠，一竄名其間，則有司不得舉手，狡者獻謀，暴者助虐，其輾轉受害者皆良民也。

translations.literal: Tianxi again said: 'The Inner Works Office supplies repairs only; in recent years it constantly says "imperial front," and old wicked clerks of corrupt deeds, fierce culprits whose tracks were pursued—once one is hidden in its name, then the proper offices cannot act; the crafty offer schemes, the violent aid oppression, and those who suffer in the round are all good people.'
translations.idiomatic: Tianxi said again: 'The Inner Works Office was meant only for palace repairs; lately it constantly invokes the "imperial front," and corrupt old clerks and tracked-down criminals are hidden under its name so that regular offices cannot act—the crafty plot, the violent help oppress, and good people are the ones who suffer.'

sentences.zh: 願毋使史臣書之曰：'內司之橫自今始。

translations.literal: May Your Majesty not let the historians write: "The Inner Office's arrogance begins from today."'
translations.idiomatic: 'Do not let the historians write that the Inner Office's arrogance began today.'

sentences.zh: '」疏上至六七，最後請還御史印，謂：「明君當爲後人除害，不當留患以遺後人。

translations.literal: When memorials reached six or seven, at last he asked to return the censor's seal, saying: 'A bright ruler should remove harm for posterity, not leave calamity to posterity.'
translations.idiomatic: When his memorials had reached six or seven, he at last asked to return the censor's seal, saying: 'A wise ruler removes harm for those who come after; he does not leave calamity for them.'

sentences.zh: 今朝廷輕給舍台諫，輕百司庶府，而北司獨重，倉卒之際，臣實懼焉。

translations.literal: Now the court lightly treats the drafting, review, and remonstrance offices and the hundred ministries, while the Northern Office alone is heavy; in a sudden crisis, your servant is truly afraid.'
translations.idiomatic: 'The court now treats the drafting, review, and remonstrance offices and the hundred ministries lightly, while the Northern Office alone is heavy; in a sudden crisis I truly fear for the realm.'

sentences.zh: 」言雖不果行，然終宋世閹人不能竊弄主威者，皆天錫之力，而天錫亦自是去朝廷矣。

translations.literal: Though his words were not carried out, yet that through the end of the Song eunuchs could not privately wield the ruler's authority was all Tianxi's doing—and Tianxi himself from this departed the court.
translations.idiomatic: Though his proposals were not fully enacted, that eunuchs could not through the rest of the Song privately wield imperial authority was largely Tianxi's doing—and from this he himself left the central court.

sentences.zh: 改大理少卿，再遷太常，皆不拜。

translations.literal: He was changed to Vice Director of the Court of Punishments, then twice promoted to Minister of Sacrifices—both declined.
translations.idiomatic: He was moved to Vice Director of Punishments, then twice offered Minister of Sacrifices—both times he declined.

sentences.zh: 改廣東提點刑獄，五辭。

translations.literal: He was changed to Guangdong judicial intendant; five times he declined.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Guangdong judicial intendant and declined five times.

sentences.zh: 明年，起知潭州，久之始至官。

translations.literal: The next year he was summoned as prefect of Tanzhou; only after a long time did he reach his post.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he was summoned as prefect of Tanzhou and only after a long delay took up the post.

sentences.zh: 戢盜賊，尊先賢，逾年大治。

translations.literal: He restrained bandits, honored former worthies, and within a year brought great order.
translations.idiomatic: He suppressed bandits, honored former worthies, and within a year brought the prefecture to good order.

sentences.zh: 直寶謨閣，遷廣東轉運判官，決疑獄，劾貪吏，治財賦，皆有法。

translations.literal: With direct appointment to the Baomo Hall, he was moved to Guangdong transport vice commissioner; he decided doubtful cases, impeached greedy officials, and managed finances—all with method.
translations.idiomatic: With direct Baomo Hall appointment he became Guangdong transport vice commissioner; he decided doubtful cases, impeached corrupt officials, and managed finances—all by sound methods.

sentences.zh: 召爲秘書監兼侍講，以聵辭，升秘閣修撰、福建轉運副使，又辭。

translations.literal: He was summoned as Director of the Secretariat with concurrent Lecturer; citing deafness he declined, was promoted to Secretariat Compiler and Fujian transport vice commissioner, and again declined.
translations.idiomatic: Recalled as Director of the Secretariat and Lecturer, he pleaded deafness and declined; promoted to Secretariat compiler and Fujian transport vice commissioner, he declined again.

sentences.zh: 度宗即位，以侍御史兼侍讀召，累辭，不許，在道間，監察御史張桂劾罷之。

translations.literal: When Emperor Duzong took the throne, he was summoned as Attendant Censor with concurrent Lecturer; repeatedly he declined and was not permitted; on the road, Supervising Censor Zhang Gui impeached and dismissed him.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Duzong ascended the throne Tianxi was summoned as Attendant Censor and Lecturer; he declined again and again but was not allowed; on the way Supervising Censor Zhang Gui impeached him and ended the appointment.

sentences.zh: 乃疏所欲對病民五事：曰公田，曰關子，曰銀綱，曰鹽鈔，曰賦役。

translations.literal: He then memorialized the five matters he wished to address for the people's illness: public fields, guanzi notes, silver convoys, salt certificates, and tax corvée.
translations.idiomatic: He then memorialized the five afflictions of the people he wished to address: public fields, guanzi notes, silver convoys, salt certificates, and tax corvée.

sentences.zh: 又言：「在廷無嚴憚之士，何以寢奸謀？

translations.literal: He also said: 'With no men of stern awe at court, how may wicked schemes be stilled? With no ministers who dare remonstrate in affairs, how may great integrity be upheld? Men are sparse, spirit enervated; many hide their laziness and spare themselves, few forget themselves and serve the state.'
translations.idiomatic: He also said: 'Without men of stern awe at court, how can wicked plots be quieted? Without ministers who dare remonstrate when crisis comes, how can great integrity be upheld? Talent is thin and spirits slack; many spare themselves, few forget themselves for the state.'

sentences.zh: 遇事無敢諍之臣，何以臨大節？

translations.literal: Promoted to Vice Minister of Works with concurrent direct appointment to the Academy of Scholars, added as Awaiting Commissioner of the Xianwen Hall, Hunan pacification commissioner, and prefect of Tanzhou; change to Tanzhou—all firmly declined.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to Vice Minister of Works with concurrent Academy of Scholars appointment, made Awaiting Commissioner of the Xianwen Hall, Hunan pacification commissioner, and prefect of Tanzhou—every post firmly declined.

sentences.zh: 人物稀疏，精采銷耎，隱惰惜已者多，忘身徇國者少。

translations.literal: The next year again he was made Fujian pacification commissioner; he firmly declined and was not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was again made Fujian pacification commissioner; he declined firmly but was not allowed.

sentences.zh: 」進工部侍郎兼直學士院，加顯文閣待制、湖南安撫使、知潭州，改潭州，皆力辭。

translations.literal: Salt-shop households who bought salt until families were ruined and lives lost—Tianxi was first to abolish it; the people held Buddhist services in gratitude.
translations.idiomatic: When salt-shop households had been ruined and even killed by compulsory salt purchases, Tianxi was the first to abolish the practice; the people held Buddhist rites in thanks.

sentences.zh: 又明年，改福建安撫使，力辭，不許。

translations.literal: He abolished the lychee tribute.
translations.idiomatic: He abolished the lychee tribute.

sentences.zh: 亭戶買鹽至破家隕身者，天錫首罷之，民作佛事以報。

translations.literal: Where saltern households bought salt until families were ruined and lives lost, Tianxi was the first to abolish the practice; the people held Buddhist services in gratitude.
translations.idiomatic: Where buying salt had ruined saltern households and cost lives, Tianxi was first to abolish it; the people held Buddhist rites to thank him.

sentences.zh: 罷荔枝貢。

translations.literal: He abolished the lychee tribute.
translations.idiomatic: He ended the lychee tribute.

sentences.zh: 召爲刑部尚書，詔憲守之臣趣行無虛日，不起。

translations.literal: He was summoned as Minister of Punishments; the edict urged the frontier guardian to hasten day by day without idle days—he did not rise to go.
translations.idiomatic: Summoned as Minister of Punishments, he was urged by edict day after day to hurry—he did not go.

sentences.zh: 久之，進顯文閣直學士，提舉太平興國宮，三降御劄趣之，又力辭。

translations.literal: After a long time he was advanced to Direct Academician of the Xianwen Hall, director of the Taiping Xingguo Palace; three times the imperial note urged him; again he firmly declined.
translations.idiomatic: After a long interval he was made Direct Academician of the Xianwen Hall and director of the Taiping Xingguo Palace; three imperial notes urged him on, and again he firmly declined.

sentences.zh: 逾年，進華文閣直學士，仍舊宮觀，尋致仕，加端明殿學士，轉一官。

translations.literal: After a year he was advanced to Direct Academician of the Huawen Hall, still at the same palace; soon he retired, was given Duanming Hall academician, and promoted one rank.
translations.idiomatic: A year later he was made Direct Academician of the Huawen Hall at the same palace; soon he retired, was given Duanming Hall academician, and promoted one rank.

sentences.zh: 疾革，草遺表以規君相。

translations.literal: When his illness grew critical, he drafted a death memorial to admonish ruler and ministers.
translations.idiomatic: As his illness turned grave, he drafted a death memorial to counsel ruler and ministers.

sentences.zh: 上震悼，特贈正議大夫，諡文毅。

translations.literal: The emperor was shaken and grieved, and specially posthumously conferred the title Grand Master of Corrective Discussion; his posthumous name was Wenyi.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was deeply shaken and grieved, and specially conferred posthumously the title Grand Master of Corrective Discussion; he was given the posthumous name Wenyi.

sentences.zh: 天錫言動有準繩，居官清介，臨事是非不可回折。

translations.literal: Tianxi in word and deed had standards; in office he was pure and firm; facing affairs, right and wrong could not be bent.
translations.idiomatic: Tianxi's words and acts had their measure; in office he was pure and unyielding; on matters of right and wrong he could not be turned aside.

sentences.zh: 所著奏議、《經筵講義》，《進故事》、《通祀輯略》、《味言發墨》、《陽岩文集》。

translations.literal: Works written include Memorials, Classics Lectures, Presenting Historical Cases, Comprehensive Sacrificial Summary, Flavorful Words Issuing Ink, and the Yangyan Collection.
translations.idiomatic: His writings include Memorials, Classics Lectures, Presenting Historical Cases, Comprehensive Sacrificial Summary, Flavorful Words Issuing Ink, and the Yangyan Collection.

sentences.zh: 黃師雍

translations.literal: Huang Shiyong
translations.idiomatic: Huang Shiyong

sentences.zh: 黃師雍，字子敬，福州人。

translations.literal: Huang Shiyong, style name Zijing, was a man of Fuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Shiyong, courtesy name Zijing, was from Fuzhou.

sentences.zh: 少從黃斡學。

translations.literal: In youth he studied with Huang Gan.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he studied under Huang Gan.

sentences.zh: 入太學。

translations.literal: He entered the Imperial University.
translations.idiomatic: He entered the Imperial University.

sentences.zh: 寶慶二年，舉進士。

translations.literal: In the second year of Baoqing he passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Baoqing (1226) he passed the jinshi examination.

sentences.zh: 詔爲楚州官屬。

translations.literal: He was ordered as an official of Chuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed to an official post in Chuzhou.

sentences.zh: 出盜賊白刃之沖，不畏不懾。

translations.literal: He went out into the very clash of bandits' naked blades, unafraid and unshaken.
translations.idiomatic: He went out into the very teeth of bandit blades and was neither afraid nor shaken.

sentences.zh: 李全反狀已露，師雍密結忠義軍別部都統時青圖之，謀泄，全殺青，師雍不爲動，全亦不加害。

translations.literal: Li Quan's rebellious intent had already shown; Shiyong secretly joined with Shi Qing of the Loyal Righteous Army's separate command to plot against him; the plot leaked, Quan killed Qing, yet Shiyong was unmoved and Quan also did not harm him.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Quan's rebellion was already plain, Shiyong secretly allied with Shi Qing, commander of a separate Loyal Righteous Army detachment, to plot against him; the plot leaked and Quan killed Qing, yet Shiyong did not flinch and Quan did not harm him either.

sentences.zh: 秩滿，朝議褒異，師雍恥出史彌遠門，不往見之。

translations.literal: When his term ended, court discussion praised him as exceptional; Shiyong was ashamed to have come out from Shi Miyuan's door and did not go to see him.
translations.idiomatic: When his term ended the court praised him as exceptional; Shiyong was ashamed to be counted among Shi Miyuan's protégés and did not go to see him.

sentences.zh: 調婺州教授，學政一以呂祖謙爲法。

translations.literal: He was transferred as professor of Wuzhou; in academic administration he took Lü Zuqian's methods as his sole model.
translations.idiomatic: Transferred as professor of Wuzhou, he ran the school wholly on Lü Zuqian's methods.

sentences.zh: 李完勉、趙必願、趙汝談皆薦之。

translations.literal: Li Wanmian, Zhao Biyuan, and Zhao Rudan all recommended him.
translations.idiomatic: Li Wanmian, Zhao Biyuan, and Zhao Rudan all recommended him.

sentences.zh: 師雍慕徐僑有清望，欲謁之，會其有召命，師雍曰：「今不可往也。

translations.literal: Shiyong admired Xu Qiao's pure reputation and wished to call on him; it happened that Qiao received a summons, and Shiyong said: 'Now is not the time to go.'
translations.idiomatic: Shiyong admired Xu Qiao's clean reputation and wished to visit him; when Qiao received a court summons Shiyong said: 'This is not the time to call on him.'

sentences.zh: 」僑聞而賢之，至闕，以其學最聞，宗勉在政府，力言于丞相喬行簡，行簡已許以朝除。

translations.literal: Qiao heard and regarded him as worthy; arriving at court, his learning was most renowned; Wanmian was in the government and spoke forcefully to Chief Councillor Qiao Xingjian, and Xingjian had already agreed to a court appointment.
translations.idiomatic: Qiao heard of it and thought him worthy; when Shiyong reached court his learning was the most talked of; Wanmian, then in government, urged Chief Councillor Qiao Xingjian, who had already agreed to a central appointment.

sentences.zh: 師雍以書見行簡，勸其歸老，行簡不悅，宗勉之請遂格。

translations.literal: Shiyong by letter saw Xingjian and urged him to retire; Xingjian was displeased, and Wanmian's request was then blocked.
translations.idiomatic: Shiyong wrote to Xingjian urging him to retire; displeased, Xingjian blocked Wanmian's recommendation.

sentences.zh: 知遂之龍溪，轉運使王伯大上其邑最。

translations.literal: He became magistrate of Longxi in Suizhou; Transport Commissioner Wang Boda reported his county as foremost.
translations.idiomatic: As magistrate of Longxi in Suizhou he was reported by Transport Commissioner Wang Boda as the foremost county.

sentences.zh: 行簡罷，宗勉與史嵩之入相，召師雍審察，將至而宗勉卒。

translations.literal: When Xingjian was dismissed, Wanmian and Shi Songzhi entered the chancellorship; Shiyong was summoned for examination and was about to arrive when Wanmian died.
translations.idiomatic: When Xingjian fell, Wanmian and Shi Songzhi came to power; Shiyong was summoned for examination and was about to reach the capital when Wanmian died.

sentences.zh: 嵩之延師雍，密示相親意，師雍不領；

translations.literal: Songzhi invited Shiyong and secretly showed intent of close kinship; Shiyong did not acknowledge it;
translations.idiomatic: Songzhi invited Shiyong and secretly signaled favor; Shiyong would not acknowledge it;

sentences.zh: 遷糧料院，又曰：「料院與相府密邇，所以相處。

translations.literal: he was moved to the Grain Provisioning Institute, and again said: 'The Grain Institute is close to the chief councillor's office—that is how one is treated.'
translations.idiomatic: he was moved to the Grain Provisioning Institute and said again: 'The Grain Institute lies next to the chief councillor's office—that is how one is handled.'

sentences.zh: 」師雍亦不領。

translations.literal: Shiyong again did not acknowledge it.
translations.idiomatic: Again Shiyong would not acknowledge it.

sentences.zh: 嵩之獨相，權勢浸盛，上下懼禍，未有發其奸者。

translations.literal: Songzhi alone held the chancellorship; power daily grew; above and below feared calamity, yet none exposed his wickedness.
translations.idiomatic: Songzhi held the chancellorship alone; his power grew daily; court and country feared disaster, yet no one exposed his crimes.

sentences.zh: 博士劉應起首疏論嵩之，帝感悟，思逐嵩之。

translations.literal: Erudite Liu Yingqi was first to memorialize attacking Songzhi; the Emperor was moved and thought to expel Songzhi.
translations.idiomatic: Erudite Liu Yingqi was the first to memorialize against Songzhi; the emperor was moved and thought to drive him out.

sentences.zh: 師雍與應起相善，故嵩之疑師雍左右之，諷御史梅杞擊師雍，差知興化軍，旋奪之，改知邵武軍。

translations.literal: Shiyong was friendly with Yingqi, so Songzhi suspected Shiyong of supporting him on either side; he hinted to Censor Mei Qi to attack Shiyong, assigning him prefect of Xinghua Commandery, soon seizing it, and changing him to prefect of Shaowu Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Shiyong was close to Yingqi, so Songzhi suspected Shiyong of aiding him and prompted Censor Mei Qi to attack him; Shiyong was sent to Xinghua, soon stripped of that post, then made prefect of Shaowu.

sentences.zh: 及應起爲監察御史，師雍遷宗正寺簿，尋亦拜監察御史。

translations.literal: When Yingqi became Supervising Censor, Shiyong was moved to Registrar of the Imperial Clan Court, and soon also appointed Supervising Censor.
translations.idiomatic: When Yingqi became Supervising Censor, Shiyong was made registrar of the Imperial Clan Court and soon after Supervising Censor.

sentences.zh: 首疏削金淵秩，送外居住。

translations.literal: His first memorial stripped Jin Yuan of rank and sent him to reside outside.
translations.idiomatic: His first memorial stripped Jin Yuan of rank and sent him to live in exile.

sentences.zh: 再疏斥趙綸、項容孫、史肯之。

translations.literal: A second memorial expelled Zhao Lun, Xiang Rongsun, and Shi Kenzhi.
translations.idiomatic: A second memorial expelled Zhao Lun, Xiang Rongsun, and Shi Kenzhi.

sentences.zh: 嵩之終喪，正言李昴英、殿中侍御史章琰共疏乞竄斥之，師雍亦上疏論列，帝感悟，即其日詔勒令致仕。

translations.literal: When Songzhi's mourning ended, Remonstrator Li Angying and Palace Attendant Censor Zhang Yan together memorialized begging his banishment; Shiyong also submitted a memorial of indictment; the Emperor was moved and that very day issued an edict ordering forced retirement.
translations.idiomatic: When Songzhi's mourning ended, Remonstrator Li Angying and Palace Attendant Censor Zhang Yan jointly begged his banishment; Shiyong also indicted him; moved, the emperor that very day ordered him to retire.

sentences.zh: 權直舍人院劉克莊封還詞頭，乞畀嵩之以貼職如宰臣去國故事，遂得守金紫光祿大夫、觀文殿學士致仕。

translations.literal: Acting in the Academy of Scholars Liu Kezhuang returned the draft edict, begging that Songzhi be given an attached office according to the precedent when a chief minister leaves court, and so he was allowed to retire as Grand Guardian of the Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon and Academician of the Observatory Hall.
translations.idiomatic: Acting in the Academy Liu Kezhuang returned the draft edict, asking that Songzhi be given an attached rank by the precedent for a departing chief minister, and so he was allowed to retire as Grand Guardian of the Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon and Academician of the Observatory Hall.

sentences.zh: 議者曰：「大夫，官也。

translations.literal: Critics said: 'Grand Guardian is an office.'
translations.idiomatic: Critics said: 'Grand Guardian is an office.'

sentences.zh: 觀文，職也。

translations.literal: Observatory Hall is a post.'
translations.idiomatic: Observatory Hall is a post.'

sentences.zh: 元降御筆但云'守官'，無'本官職'之辭。

translations.literal: The original imperial brush only said "guard office," without the words "original office and post."'
translations.idiomatic: The original imperial note said only "guard office," not "original office and post."

sentences.zh: 觀文之命，自克莊啟之。

translations.literal: The Observatory Hall appointment was opened by Kezhuang.'
translations.idiomatic: The Observatory Hall appointment began with Kezhuang.'

sentences.zh: 朋邪顧望，不可赦。

translations.literal: Factional wickedness looking back—cannot be pardoned.'
translations.idiomatic: Such partisan favor looking backward cannot be forgiven.'

sentences.zh: 」師雍遂劾克莊臨事失身犯義，免所居官，琰亦繼劾克莊，師雍又乞籍嵩之家隸張叔儀，皆從之。

translations.literal: Shiyong then impeached Kezhuang for losing integrity and violating righteousness in the affair, and removed him from office; Yan also followed in impeaching Kezhuang; Shiyong again begged to register Songzhi's household slave Zhang Shuyi—all were granted.
translations.idiomatic: Shiyong then impeached Kezhuang for compromising himself in the affair and had him removed; Yan also impeached Kezhuang; Shiyong again asked to register Songzhi's household slave Zhang Shuyi—all were granted.

sentences.zh: 未幾，昴英劾臨安尹趙與𥲅及執政，琰亦劾執政，帝怒昴英並及琰。

translations.literal: Before long Angying impeached the prefect of Lin'an Zhao Yuchou and the chief ministers; Yan also impeached the chief ministers; the Emperor was angry at Angying and implicated Yan.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Angying impeached the Lin'an prefect Zhao Yuchou and the chief ministers; Yan also impeached the chief ministers; the emperor's anger at Angying swept up Yan as well.

sentences.zh: 鄭采乘間劾琰、昴英，又嗾同列再疏，以昴英屬某人，琰屬師雍。

translations.literal: Zheng Cai seized the moment to impeach Yan and Angying, and also urged his colleagues to submit another memorial, saying Angying belonged to a certain man and Yan belonged to Shiyong.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Cai seized the moment to impeach Yan and Angying, and also urged his colleagues to memorialize again, claiming Angying belonged to one faction and Yan to Shiyong.

sentences.zh: 師雍毅然不從，獨擊葉閶乃與𥲅腹心。

translations.literal: Shiyong resolutely would not comply, attacking Ye Chang alone as a confidant of Yu'e.
translations.idiomatic: Shiyong stood firm and refused to go along, singling out Ye Chang as a trusted inner ally of Zhao Yu'e.

sentences.zh: 琰、昴英去國，采於是薦周坦、葉大有入台，首劾程公許、江萬里，善類日危矣。

translations.literal: Yan and Angying left the court; Cai thereupon recommended Zhou Tan and Ye Dayou to enter the Censorate, first impeaching Cheng Gongxu and Jiang Wanli—the upright faction grew more imperiled by the day.
translations.idiomatic: With Yan and Angying driven from court, Cai now advanced Zhou Tan and Ye Dayou into the Censorate, opening with impeachments of Cheng Gongxu and Jiang Wanli, and men of integrity found themselves in daily greater peril.

sentences.zh: 未逾月，坦攻參政吳潛去，陳垓爲監察御史，時采、與𥲅、坦、垓、大有合爲一，師雍獨立。

translations.literal: Within less than a month Tan attacked Vice Administrator Wu Qian into removal; Chen Gai became Investigating Censor. At that time Cai, Yu'e, Tan, Gai, and Dayou had merged into one bloc, while Shiyong stood alone.
translations.idiomatic: In less than a month Tan had hounded Vice Administrator Wu Qian from office, and Chen Gai took up the post of Investigating Censor. Cai, Zhao Yu'e, Tan, Gai, and Dayou now moved as a single faction, with Shiyong the sole holdout.

sentences.zh: 采惡之尤甚，思所以去師雍，未得，招四人共謀之。

translations.literal: Cai hated him all the more, scheming how to remove Shiyong but not succeeding; he summoned the four to plot together.
translations.idiomatic: Cai loathed him all the more and cast about for a way to drive Shiyong out, yet could not manage it, and so called the four of them into joint counsel.

sentences.zh: 會大旱求言，應招者多指采、坦等爲起災之由，牟子才、李伯玉、盧鉞語尤峻。

translations.literal: It happened that in a great drought the throne sought remonstrance; many who responded pointed to Cai, Tan, and others as the cause of the calamity, and the words of Mou Zicai, Li Boyu, and Lu Yue were especially severe.
translations.idiomatic: When a severe drought prompted the court to invite criticism, most memorialists named Cai, Tan, and their circle as the source of the disaster, and the language of Mou Zicai, Li Boyu, and Lu Yue was especially cutting.

sentences.zh: 坦等偽撰匿名書，誣三士，師雍榻前辨，謂：「匿名書條令所禁，非公論也，不知何爲至前。

translations.literal: Tan and the rest forged anonymous letters to slander the three gentlemen. Shiyong argued before the throne, saying: "Anonymous letters are forbidden by statute—they are not public opinion. I do not know why they have been brought here."
translations.idiomatic: Tan and his allies forged anonymous libels against the three scholars. Shiyong rebutted them at the imperial couch, saying, "Anonymous writings are barred by law; they are not the voice of public judgment—why have they been laid before Your Majesty?"

sentences.zh: 」因發其偽撰之跡。

translations.literal: "—and thereby exposed the trail of their forgery.
translations.idiomatic: He thereby laid bare the evidence of their fabrication.

sentences.zh: 適鉞疏譽師雍，采乃以鉞附師雍，帝不聽，擢師雍左司諫。

translations.literal: Just then Yue memorialized in praise of Shiyong; Cai then attached Yue to Shiyong, but the Emperor would not listen and promoted Shiyong to Left Office Remonstrator.
translations.idiomatic: At that moment Lu Yue submitted a memorial commending Shiyong; Cai tried to lump Yue together with him, but the Emperor would not heed it and promoted Shiyong to Left Office Remonstrator.

sentences.zh: 未幾，采入政府，謝方叔、趙汝騰疏其奸，采遂罷去。

translations.literal: Before long Cai entered the government; Xie Fangshu and Zhao Ruteng memorialized his treachery, and Cai was thereupon dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Cai took a seat in the central government, but Xie Fangshu and Zhao Ruteng exposed his misconduct in memorials, and he was soon removed.

sentences.zh: 師雍與丞相鄭清之故同舍，然以劾劉用行、魏峴皆清之親故，清之不樂。

translations.literal: Shiyong and Chief Councillor Zheng Qingzhi had once been fellow lodgers, yet because he impeached Liu Yongxing and Wei Xian—both Qingzhi's kin and associates—Qingzhi was displeased.
translations.idiomatic: Shiyong and Chief Councillor Zheng Qingzhi had once roomed together as students, yet his impeachments of Liu Yongxing and Wei Xian—both men tied to Qingzhi by kinship and friendship—had left the chief councillor ill at ease.

sentences.zh: 坦喜曰：「吾得所以去之矣。

translations.literal: Tan rejoiced, saying: "I have found the means to remove him."
translations.idiomatic: Tan exulted, saying, "I have found the way to get rid of him."

sentences.zh: 」遣其婦日造清之妻，譖曰：「彼去用行、峴，乃去丞相之漸也。

translations.literal: He sent his wife day after day to visit Qingzhi's wife, slandering: "His removal of Yongxing and Xian is but the first step toward removing the chief councillor."
translations.idiomatic: He sent his wife daily to call on Qingzhi's wife with insinuations: "When he drove out Yongxing and Xian, he was only clearing the path to oust the chief councillor."

sentences.zh: 」帝將以師雍爲侍御史，清之曰：「如此，則臣不可留。

translations.literal: The Emperor was about to appoint Shiyong Attending Censor; Qingzhi said: "If that is done, then your servant cannot remain."
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor was on the point of naming Shiyong Attending Censor, but Qingzhi said, "If that appointment stands, then this subject cannot stay in office."

sentences.zh: 」遷起居舍人兼侍講，即力丐去。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Gentleman Attendant who Drafts Imperial Documents and concurrent Court Lecturer, and at once pressed strenuously to resign.
translations.idiomatic: Shiyong was shifted to Gentleman Attendant who Drafts Imperial Documents with a concurrent post as Court Lecturer, and immediately pleaded with all his strength to be released.

sentences.zh: 清之猶冀師雍少貶，師雍曰：「吾欲爲全人。

translations.literal: Qingzhi still hoped Shiyong would accept a slight demotion; Shiyong said: "I wish to be a whole man."
translations.idiomatic: Qingzhi still hoped Shiyong might accept a modest demotion; Shiyong replied, "I mean to remain a man whole and unbroken."

sentences.zh: 」終不屈。

translations.literal: In the end he would not bend.
translations.idiomatic: In the end he would not yield.

sentences.zh: 數月，坦卒劾師雍及高斯得俱罷。

translations.literal: Several months later Tan at last impeached Shiyong and Gao Side together into dismissal.
translations.idiomatic: Several months later Tan finally secured the dismissal of both Shiyong and Gao Side through impeachment.

sentences.zh: 久之，以直寶文閣奉祠，陳垓又嗾同列寢之。

translations.literal: After a long while he was appointed Direct Gentleman for the Compilation of Exalted Literary Works with temple service stipend; Chen Gai again incited his colleagues to bury him in silence.
translations.idiomatic: Long afterward he was given the title Direct Gentleman for the Compilation of Exalted Literary Works with a temple-service stipend, and Chen Gai once more urged his colleagues to smother any word on his behalf.

sentences.zh: 清之卒，起師雍爲左史，既而改江西轉運使，遷禮部侍郎，命下而卒於江西官舍。

translations.literal: When Qingzhi died, Shiyong was raised to Left Historiographer, then changed to Jiangxi Transport Commissioner, promoted to Vice Minister of Rites—the order issued, and he died in the Jiangxi official residence.
translations.idiomatic: After Qingzhi's death Shiyong was recalled as Left Historiographer, then appointed Jiangxi Transport Commissioner and promoted to Vice Minister of Rites; the appointment reached him only to find him already dead in his Jiangxi quarters.

sentences.zh: 師雍簡淡寡欲，靖厚有守，言若不出口，而於邪正之辨甚明，視外物輕甚，故博采公論，當官而行，愛護名節，無愧師友云。

translations.literal: Shiyong was plain and sparing in desire, steady and principled, speaking as if words scarcely left his mouth, yet exceedingly clear in distinguishing wrong from right, holding external things very light; therefore he gathered broad public opinion, acted in office as duty required, cherished his name and integrity, and had no cause to blush before teachers and friends.
translations.idiomatic: Shiyong lived simply, with few wants, and was grave, steadfast, and principled—so sparing of speech that he seemed hardly to speak at all, yet razor-clear in telling right from wrong and utterly indifferent to outward gain. He weighed the broad consensus of opinion, did in office what office demanded, and guarded his reputation and integrity without shame before his teachers and friends.

sentences.zh: 徐元傑

translations.literal: Xu Yuanjie
translations.idiomatic: Xu Yuanjie

sentences.zh: 徐元傑，字仁伯，信州上饒人。

translations.literal: Xu Yuanjie, styled Renbo, was a man of Shangrao in Xin Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Yuanjie, courtesy name Renbo, came from Shangrao in Xin Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 幼穎悟，誦書日數千言，每冥思精索。

translations.literal: As a child he was sharp and perceptive; he recited books at several thousand characters a day, each time plumbing the text in deep thought.
translations.idiomatic: Even as a boy he was quick and penetrating; he could recite several thousand characters of text in a day, and would brood over each passage until he had grasped its marrow.

sentences.zh: 聞陳文蔚講書鉛山，實朱熹門人，往師之。

translations.literal: Hearing that Chen Wenwei lectured on the classics at Qianshan—a true disciple of Zhu Xi—he went to study under him.
translations.idiomatic: Learning that Chen Wenwei was lecturing at Qianshan and was a genuine disciple of Zhu Xi, he went to become his student.

sentences.zh: 後師事真德秀。

translations.literal: Later he took Zhen Dexiu as his teacher.
translations.idiomatic: He later studied under Zhen Dexiu as well.

sentences.zh: 紹定五年，進士及第。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Shaoding he passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Shaoding he passed the jinshi examinations.

sentences.zh: 簽書鎮東軍節判官廳公事。

translations.literal: He signed documents as an official of the Eastern Garrison Military Commission.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed to sign documents in the Eastern Garrison Military Commission.

sentences.zh: 嘉熙二年，召爲秘書省正字，遷校書郎。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jiaxi he was summoned as Rectifier of Documents in the Secretariat, and promoted to Collator.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Jiaxi he was summoned to the Secretariat as Rectifier of Documents and soon promoted to Collator.

sentences.zh: 奏否泰、剝復之理，因及右轄久虛，非骨鯁耆艾，身足負荷斯世者，不可輕畀。

translations.literal: He memorialized on the principles of adversity and prosperity, decay and renewal, and thereby on the long vacancy at the right vice-rank—only a man of bone and spine, aged and venerable, whose person could bear the weight of the age, ought not be lightly bestowed.
translations.idiomatic: He submitted a memorial on the cycles of adversity and prosperity, decay and renewal, and argued that the long-standing vacancy at the right vice-rank ought not be filled lightly: only a man of moral backbone, seasoned and venerable, whose shoulders could truly carry the age was fit for such an appointment.

sentences.zh: 又言皇子竑當置後及蚤立太子，乞蚤定大計。

translations.literal: He also said that the prince Qi ought to be provided an heir and that the heir apparent should be established early, begging that the great design be settled soon.
translations.idiomatic: He also urged that Prince Qi be given an heir and that the crown prince be named without delay, pleading for an early settlement of the succession.

sentences.zh: 時諫官蔣峴方力排竑置後之說，遂力請外，不許，即謁告歸，丐祠，章十二上。

translations.literal: At that time the remonstrator Jiang Yan was vigorously opposing the proposal to establish an heir for Qi; Yuanjie thereupon pressed strenuously for an outside post, was not permitted, immediately requested leave to return, and begged a temple stipend—twelve memorials in all.
translations.idiomatic: The remonstrator Jiang Yan was then fiercely opposing any heir for Prince Qi, so Yuanjie pressed all the harder for an outside appointment. When the court refused, he took leave to return home and petitioned repeatedly for a temple stipend—twelve memorials in all.

sentences.zh: 三年，遷著作佐郎兼兵部郎官，以疾辭。

translations.literal: In the third year he was promoted to Assistant Compiler and concurrent Lang Official of the Ministry of War, and resigned on grounds of illness.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he was promoted to Assistant Compiler with a concurrent post in the Ministry of War, but resigned citing illness.

sentences.zh: 差知安吉州，辭。

translations.literal: He was assigned to know Anji Prefecture and declined.
translations.idiomatic: He was ordered to serve as prefect of Anji but declined.

sentences.zh: 召赴行在奏事，辭益堅。

translations.literal: Summoned to the capital to report on affairs, he declined all the more firmly.
translations.idiomatic: When summoned to the capital to present himself on state affairs, he refused with still greater resolve.

sentences.zh: 丞相史嵩之丁父憂，有詔起復，中外莫敢言，惟學校叩閽力爭。

translations.literal: Chief Councillor Shi Songzhi was in mourning for his father; an edict ordered his recall to office, and at court and beyond none dared speak—only the schools battered the palace gates in strenuous protest.
translations.idiomatic: When Chief Councillor Shi Songzhi was mourning his father, an edict recalled him to office before the mourning term had ended. Throughout court and country none dared object openly, but the academies alone stormed the palace gates in fierce protest.

sentences.zh: 元傑時適輪對，言：「臣前日晉侍經筵，親承聖問以大臣史嵩之起復，臣奏陛下出命太輕，人言不可沮抑。

translations.literal: When Yuanjie came up in rotation to face the throne he said: "Your servant the other day attended the classics lecture at the palace and personally received the Sacred Inquiry concerning the great minister Shi Songzhi's recall from mourning; your servant memorialized that Your Majesty's issuance of the order was too light and that human opinion could not be suppressed."
translations.idiomatic: When Yuanjie's turn came to address the throne he said, "Your servant recently attended the classics lecture and heard Your Majesty's own inquiry regarding the recall of the great minister Shi Songzhi from mourning. I answered that the command had been issued too lightly and that public opinion could not simply be stifled."

sentences.zh: 陛下自盡陛下之禮，大臣自盡大臣之禮，玉音賜俞，臣又何所容喙。

translations.literal: "Your Majesty should fully perform Your Majesty's rites, and the great minister should fully perform the great minister's rites; the jade voice granted assent—what more could your servant add?"
translations.idiomatic: "Let Your Majesty fulfill every rite owed by the throne, and let the great minister fulfill every rite owed by a minister—the imperial voice assented, and what more was there for your servant to say?"

sentences.zh: 今觀學校之書，使人感歎。

translations.literal: Now reading the schools' letters moves one to sigh.
translations.idiomatic: Yet to read the petitions from the schools now is enough to move one to tears.

sentences.zh: 且大臣讀聖賢之書，畏天命，畏人言。

translations.literal: Moreover, great ministers read the books of the sages, fear Heaven's mandate, and fear human speech.
translations.idiomatic: Great ministers, after all, study the books of the sages; they fear Heaven's mandate and they fear the judgment of men.

sentences.zh: 家庭之變，哀戚終事，禮制有常。

translations.literal: When calamity strikes the family, grief and mourning must run their course—ritual has its constant rule.
translations.idiomatic: When disaster visits the household, grief and mourning must be seen to the end; the rites prescribe what is fixed.

sentences.zh: 臣竊料其何至於忽送死之大事，輕出以犯清議哉！

translations.literal: Your servant ventures to suppose—how could he come to neglect so grave a matter as seeing the dead properly honored and lightly step forth to offend clear public opinion!
translations.idiomatic: I cannot believe he would treat so solemn a duty as laying the dead to rest with contempt and step lightly back into office in defiance of plain public conscience!

sentences.zh: 前日昕庭出命之易，士論所以凜凜者，實以陛下爲四海綱常之主，大臣身任道揆，扶翊綱常者也。

translations.literal: The reason court opinion was so sternly chilled by the ease with which the order was issued the other day at the dawn audience is that Your Majesty is master of the moral order of all within the seas, and the great minister bears the Way and props up that moral order.
translations.idiomatic: The reason opinion at court turned so cold when the command was issued so easily at the dawn audience is simply this: Your Majesty is the guardian of the moral order under Heaven, and the great minister is charged with the Way and with upholding that order.

sentences.zh: 自聞大臣有起復之命，雖未知其避就若何，凡有父母之心者莫不失聲涕零，是果何爲而然？

translations.literal: From the moment word came of the great minister's recall from mourning, though none yet knew whether he would accept or refuse, every heart that still had a parent's heart broke into uncontrollable weeping—what in truth could cause such a thing?
translations.idiomatic: From the moment the recall was announced, though no one yet knew whether he would accept or refuse it, every man who still cherished a parent's memory wept aloud without restraint—what, in truth, could stir such grief?

sentences.zh: 人心天理，誰實無之，興言及此，非可使聞於鄰國也。

translations.literal: The human heart and Heaven's principle—who is without them? To raise the matter to this pitch is not something fit to be heard in neighboring states.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven's principle lives in every human heart—who lacks it? That the matter should rise to such a pitch is not something our neighbors ought to hear.

sentences.zh: 陛下烏得而不悔悟，大臣烏得而不堅忍？

translations.literal: How could Your Majesty fail to repent and awaken, and how could the great minister fail to stand firm and endure?
translations.idiomatic: How can Your Majesty fail to repent and awaken, and how can the great minister fail to hold firm and endure?

sentences.zh: 臣懇懇納忠，何敢詆訐，特爲陛下愛惜民彝，爲大臣愛惜名節而已。

translations.literal: Your servant earnestly offers loyal words—how would he dare slander? He speaks only to have Your Majesty cherish the people's moral nature and to have the great minister cherish his name and integrity.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant offers this loyal counsel in earnest—how would he dare calumniate anyone? He speaks only so that Your Majesty may cherish the people's moral nature and the great minister may cherish his reputation and integrity.

sentences.zh: 」疏出，朝野傳誦，帝亦察其忠亮，每從容訪天下事，以筵益申前議。

translations.literal: "—When the memorial went out, court and countryside passed it from hand to hand; the Emperor also perceived his loyalty and candor, and from time to time in easy conversation inquired about affairs under Heaven, using the lecture sessions to press the earlier argument further.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial was issued, it was copied and recited throughout court and countryside. The Emperor, too, perceived his loyalty and plain dealing, and would often in unhurried conversation ask his view of affairs under Heaven, using the lecture hall to press the earlier argument further.

sentences.zh: 未幾，夜降御筆黜四不才台諫，起復之命遂寢。

translations.literal: Before long, at night an imperial brush-note dismissed four incompetent censors and remonstrators, and the recall order was thereupon shelved.
translations.idiomatic: Before long, late one night, an imperial brush-note dismissed four incompetent censors and remonstrators, and the recall order was quietly set aside.

sentences.zh: 元老舊德次第收召，元傑亦兼右司郎官，拜太常少卿，兼給事中、國子祭酒，權中書舍人。

translations.literal: Senior veterans were summoned back in turn; Yuanjie also took a concurrent post as Right Office Lang Official, was appointed Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices with concurrent posts as Supervising Secretary, National University Rector, and Acting Drafting Attendant of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Veteran statesmen were called back to service one after another; Yuanjie was also given a concurrent post in the Right Office, appointed Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, and named concurrently Supervising Secretary, National University Rector, and Acting Drafting Attendant of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 杜範入相，復延議軍國事。

translations.literal: When Du Fan entered as chief councillor, discussion of military and state affairs was again extended to him.
translations.idiomatic: When Du Fan became chief councillor, Yuanjie was again drawn into deliberations on military and civil affairs.

sentences.zh: 爲書無慮數十，所言皆朝廷大政，邊鄙遠慮。

translations.literal: He wrote letters without number—several tens—all treating great policies of the court and far-seeing concerns of the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote dozens of letters, every one of them touching major court policy and long-range frontier concerns.

sentences.zh: 每裁書至宗社隱憂處，輒閣筆揮涕，書就隨削稿，雖子弟無有知者。

translations.literal: Whenever in drafting a letter he came to the hidden anxieties of the altars of state, he would lay down the brush and weep; when the letter was finished he at once destroyed the draft, so that even his sons and younger brothers never knew.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he reached in writing those passages that voiced the dynasty's unspoken dread, he would set down the brush and weep; once the letter was done he destroyed the draft at once, so that not even his sons knew what he had written.

sentences.zh: 六月朔，輪當侍立，以暴疾謁告。

translations.literal: On the first day of the sixth month, when his turn came to attend in attendance, he requested leave on account of a sudden illness.
translations.idiomatic: On the first day of the sixth month, when his rotation required him to attend at the throne, he begged leave, claiming a sudden illness.

sentences.zh: 特拜工部侍郎，隨乞納，詔轉一官致仕。

translations.literal: He was specially appointed Vice Minister of Works, and at once petitioned to decline acceptance; an edict transferred him one rank and granted retirement.
translations.idiomatic: He was specially promoted to Vice Minister of Works, but immediately petitioned to refuse the appointment; the court then advanced him one rank and granted retirement.

sentences.zh: 夜四鼓。

translations.literal: At the fourth watch of the night.
translations.idiomatic: At the fourth watch of the night.

sentences.zh: 遂卒。

translations.literal: He thereupon died.
translations.idiomatic: He died.

sentences.zh: 先，元傑未死之一日，方謁左丞相范鐘歸，又折簡察院劉應起，將以冀日奏事。

translations.literal: Earlier, on the day before Yuanjie died, he had just called on Left Chief Councillor Fan Zhong on his return, and also sent a note to Liu Yingqi of the Investigation Office, intending to present himself on state affairs the next day.
translations.idiomatic: The day before his death Yuanjie had paid a visit to Left Chief Councillor Fan Zhong and, on his way home, sent a note to Liu Yingqi of the Investigation Office, planning to appear at court the following day.

sentences.zh: 是夕，俄熱大作，詰朝不能造朝，夜煩愈甚，指爪忽裂，以死。

translations.literal: That evening a sudden fever seized him with great violence; at dawn he could not go to court; through the night the affliction grew worse, his fingernails suddenly split—and he died.
translations.idiomatic: That evening a violent fever struck him; by morning he could not attend court. Through the night the illness worsened, his fingernails split open—and he was dead.

sentences.zh: 朝紳及三學諸生往吊，相顧駭泣。

translations.literal: Court gentlemen and students of the three academies came to mourn him, looking at one another in shock and weeping.
translations.idiomatic: Court officials and students of the three academies came to mourn, staring at one another in horror and tears.

sentences.zh: 訃聞，帝震悼曰：「徐元傑前日方侍立，不聞有疾，何死之遽耶？

translations.literal: When the death report arrived the Emperor was shaken and grieved, saying: "Xu Yuanjie was attending just the other day—I heard no word of illness. How could he die so suddenly?
translations.idiomatic: When word of his death arrived the Emperor was stricken with grief, saying, "Xu Yuanjie was in attendance only the other day—I heard nothing of illness. How could he die so suddenly?

sentences.zh: 」亟遣中使問狀，賻贈銀絹二百計。

translations.literal: "—He at once sent a palace envoy to inquire into the circumstances and bestowed two hundred strings of silver and silk as condolence gifts.
translations.idiomatic: He immediately dispatched a palace envoy to investigate and granted two hundred strings' worth of silver and silk as funeral gifts.

sentences.zh: 已而太學諸生伏闕訴其爲中毒，且曰：「昔小人有傾君子者，不過使之自死於蠻煙瘴雨之鄉，今蠻煙瘴雨不在領海，而在陛下之朝廷。

translations.literal: Thereafter students of the Imperial University knelt at the palace gates alleging that he had been poisoned, saying: "In old times when petty men overturned gentlemen, they did no more than make them die by their own hand in lands of miasmic vapors and pestilential rains. Today those miasmic vapors and pestilential rains are not beyond the frontier—they are within Your Majesty's court.
translations.idiomatic: Then students of the Imperial University knelt at the palace gates claiming he had been poisoned, saying, "When petty men of old destroyed gentlemen, they merely drove them to die by their own hand in frontier lands of miasma and pestilence. Today that miasma and pestilence are not beyond the seas—they are in Your Majesty's own court.

sentences.zh: 望奮發睿斷，大明典刑。

translations.literal: We look to Your Sagely resolve being roused and the canonical punishments made bright.
translations.idiomatic: We beg that your sacred resolve be roused and justice be made fully manifest.

sentences.zh: 」於是三學諸生相繼叩閽訟冤，台諫交疏論奏，監學官亦合辭聞於朝。

translations.literal: "—Thereupon students of the three academies in succession battered the palace gates to plead his wrongs; censors and remonstrators submitted memorial after memorial; the supervisory officials of the academies also jointly reported to the court.
translations.idiomatic: Students of the three academies then came in waves to batter the palace gates and plead his cause; censors and remonstrators piled memorial upon memorial; and the academies' supervisory officers jointly reported the matter to court.

sentences.zh: 二子直諒、直方乞以恤典充賞格。

translations.literal: His two sons Zhiliang and Zhifang begged that the condolence favor be applied toward an examination privilege.
translations.idiomatic: His sons Zhiliang and Zhifang asked that the funeral honors be converted into examination privileges.

sentences.zh: 有旨付臨安府逮醫者孫志甯及常所給使鞫治。

translations.literal: An order entrusted the matter to the Lin'an prefecture to arrest and try the physician Sun Zhining and the regular attendants who had served him.
translations.idiomatic: An edict referred the case to the Lin'an prefecture to arrest and try the physician Sun Zhining and his usual personal attendants.

sentences.zh: 既又改理寺，詔殿中侍御史鄭采董之，且募告者賞緡錢十萬、官初品。

translations.literal: It was then transferred to the Court of Judicial Review; an edict ordered Attending Censor Zheng Cai to supervise the case, and offered a reward of one hundred thousand cash and an entry-level office to anyone who informed.
translations.idiomatic: The case was then shifted to the Court of Judicial Review, with an edict placing Attending Censor Zheng Cai in charge and promising one hundred thousand cash and an initial-rank appointment to any informer.

sentences.zh: 大理寺正黃濤謂伏暑證，二子乞斬濤謝先臣。

translations.literal: The Court's director Huang Tao said it was a case of summer-heat affliction; the two sons begged that Tao be beheaded to appease their late father.
translations.idiomatic: The court's director Huang Tao ruled it a case of summer-heat sickness; the two sons petitioned that Tao be executed to appease their father's spirit.

sentences.zh: 然獄迄無成，海內人士傷之，帝悼念不已，賜官田五百畝、緡錢五千給其家。

translations.literal: Yet the case in the end came to nothing; men of note throughout the realm grieved for him, and the Emperor's mourning did not cease—he granted five hundred mu of official fields and five thousand strings of cash to the family.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the inquiry never reached a conclusion; scholars throughout the empire mourned him, and the Emperor's grief did not end—he granted the family five hundred mu of official land and five thousand strings of cash.

sentences.zh: 賜諡忠湣。

translations.literal: He was given the posthumous title Zhongmin.
translations.idiomatic: He was granted the posthumous title Zhongmin, "Loyal and Sorrowing."

sentences.zh: 孫子秀

translations.literal: Sun Zixiu
translations.idiomatic: Sun Zixiu

sentences.zh: 孫子秀，字元實，越州余姚人。

translations.literal: Sun Zixiu, styled Yuanshi, was a man of Yuyao in Yue Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Zixiu, courtesy name Yuanshi, came from Yuyao in Yue Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 紹定五年進士。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Shaoding he passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Shaoding he passed the jinshi examinations.

sentences.zh: 調吳縣主簿。

translations.literal: He was appointed chief clerk of Wu County.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed chief clerk of Wu County.

sentences.zh: 有妖人稱「水仙太保」，郡守王遂將使治之，莫敢行，子秀奮然請往，焚其廬，碎其像，沈其人於太湖，曰：「實汝水仙之名矣。

translations.literal: There was a sorcerer who called himself "Grand Protector of the Water Immortal"; the prefect Wang Sui was about to have him prosecuted, but none dared go; Zixiu boldly volunteered, burned his lodge, smashed his image, and drowned the man in Lake Tai, saying: "So this is the true meaning of your title as Water Immortal.
translations.idiomatic: A sorcerer styled himself "Grand Protector of the Water Immortal." Prefect Wang Sui meant to prosecute him, yet none dared act; Zixiu stepped forward boldly, burned the man's lodge, shattered his idol, and drowned him in Lake Tai, saying, "So this is what it truly means to be a water immortal.

sentences.zh: 」妖遂絕。

translations.literal: "—The sorcery thereupon ceased.
translations.idiomatic: The cult was extinguished.

sentences.zh: 日詣學宮與諸生討論義理。

translations.literal: Each day he went to the school and discussed principle with the students.
translations.idiomatic: Each day he went to the county school to debate moral principle with the students.

sentences.zh: 辟淮東總領所中酒庫，檄督宜興縣圍田租。

translations.literal: He was recruited to the Huaidong General Commissariat's central wine depot, and by dispatch supervised the encircled-field land rent of Yixing County.
translations.idiomatic: He was recruited to the Huaidong General Commissariat's central wine depot and, by special dispatch, oversaw the encircled-field land rents of Yixing County.

sentences.zh: 既還，白水災，總領恚曰：「軍餉所關，而敢若此，獨不爲身計乎？

translations.literal: When he returned, a flood struck Baishui; the general commissary raged: "Army provisions are at stake—yet you dare act like this. Do you alone not calculate for yourself?"
translations.idiomatic: On his return a flood struck Baishui. The general commissary thundered, "Army rations hang on this—how dare you behave so? Have you no thought for your own safety?"

sentences.zh: 」子秀曰：「何敢爲身計，寧罪去爾。

translations.literal: Zixiu said: "How would I dare calculate for myself? Better to accept punishment and leave."
translations.idiomatic: Zixiu replied, "How could I think only of myself? I would rather accept punishment and go."

sentences.zh: 」力爭之，遂免。

translations.literal: He argued strenuously, and the levy was thereupon remitted.
translations.idiomatic: He argued with all his force, and the exaction was waived.

sentences.zh: 調滁州教授，至官，改知金壇縣。

translations.literal: He was transferred to instructor at Chuzhou; on reaching his post he was changed to magistrate of Jintan County.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to serve as instructor at Chuzhou, and upon arrival was reassigned as magistrate of Jintan County.

sentences.zh: 嚴保伍，厘經界，結義役，一切與民休息。

translations.literal: He enforced the mutual-surveillance groups strictly, clarified land boundaries, organized corvée by covenant, and in every respect gave the people rest.
translations.idiomatic: He enforced the mutual-surveillance system rigorously, clarified land boundaries, organized corvée through neighborhood covenants, and in every way let the people breathe.

sentences.zh: 訟者使齎牒自詣裏正，並鄰證來然後行，不實者往往自匿其牒，惟豪黠者有犯，則痛繩不少貨。

translations.literal: Litigants were made to carry their writs themselves to the village chief, and only when neighboring witnesses had also come would proceedings go forward; those whose claims were false often hid their writs of their own accord—only the violent and cunning who offended were harshly punished without leniency.
translations.idiomatic: Litigants were required to bring their petitions in person to the village head, and cases moved forward only after neighbors had come to testify; the dishonest often abandoned their writs of their own accord, while only the brutal and crafty who truly offended were flogged without mercy.

sentences.zh: 淮民流入以萬計，振給撫恤，樹廬舍，括田使耕，拔其能者分治之。

translations.literal: Huai River refugees poured in by the tens of thousands; he relieved, supplied, and comforted them, erected shelters, registered fields for them to till, and promoted the capable among them to help govern.
translations.idiomatic: Refugees from the Huai region streamed in by the tens of thousands; he fed them, comforted them, built shelters, assigned fields for cultivation, and elevated the able among them to share in local administration.

sentences.zh: 崇學校，明教化，行鄉飲酒禮。

translations.literal: He honored the schools, clarified instruction and transformation, and performed the village drinking ceremony.
translations.idiomatic: He exalted the schools, made teaching and moral transformation explicit, and conducted the village drinking rite.

sentences.zh: 訪國初茅山書院故址，新之，以待遠方遊學之士。

translations.literal: He sought out the former site of the Maoshan Academy from the dynasty's founding, rebuilt it anew, and made it ready to receive traveling scholars from distant places.
translations.idiomatic: He located the Maoshan Academy's original founding site, restored it, and opened it to scholars who came from afar.

sentences.zh: 通判慶元府，主管浙東鹽事。

translations.literal: He served as vice-prefect of Qingyuan Prefecture and supervised Zhedong salt affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was made vice-prefect of Qingyuan and put in charge of Zhedong salt administration.

sentences.zh: 先是，諸場鹽百袋附五袋，名「五厘鹽」，未幾，提舉官以爲正數，民困甚，子秀奏蠲之。

translations.literal: Previously, at the salt yards every hundred bags carried an appended five bags, called the "five-li salt"; before long the intendant treated it as a regular quota, and the people were sorely burdened; Zixiu memorialized to have it remitted.
translations.idiomatic: At the salt yards every hundred bags had carried an extra five, known as the "five-li salt"; soon the intendant made that surcharge a fixed quota, and the people were crushed under it—until Zixiu memorialized for its abolition.

sentences.zh: 辟幹辦行在諸司糧料院。

translations.literal: He was summoned as a staff officer of the Liangliao Yuan among the capital agencies.
translations.idiomatic: He was recruited as a staff officer in the capital's Liangliao Yuan.

sentences.zh: 衢州冠作，水冒城郭，朝廷擇守，屬子秀行。

translations.literal: Bandit leaders rose in Quzhou and floodwaters engulfed the city walls; the court chose a magistrate and assigned Zixiu to go.
translations.idiomatic: Banditry erupted in Quzhou while floodwaters swamped the walls; the court picked a new prefect and sent Zixiu.

sentences.zh: 子秀謂捕賊之責，雖在有司，亦必習土俗之人，乃能翦其憑依，裁其奔突。

translations.literal: Zixiu said that although the duty of catching bandits lay with the authorities, only men versed in local custom could cut off their bases of support and check their sudden raids.
translations.idiomatic: Zixiu argued that catching bandits was formally the magistrate's job, yet only men who knew local ways could strip rebels of their hideouts and stop their raids.

sentences.zh: 乃立保伍，選用土豪，首旌常山縣令陳謙亨、寓士周還淳等捍禦之勞，且表於朝，乞加優賞，人心由是競勸。

translations.literal: He thereupon established baowu units and selected local strongmen; he first honored Magistrate Chen Qianheng of Changshan and resident scholar Zhou Huanchun for their labors in defense, memorialized the court to grant them extra rewards, and popular zeal for emulation followed.
translations.idiomatic: He set up baowu militia and enlisted local strongmen, first commending Changshan magistrate Chen Qianheng and resident scholar Zhou Huanchun for holding the line, then petitioned the court for special rewards—whereupon everyone rushed to follow their example.

sentences.zh: 未幾，盜復起江山、玉山間，甫七日，而衆禽四十八人以來。

translations.literal: Before long bandits rose again between Jiangshan and Yushan; within only seven days forty-eight captives were brought in.
translations.idiomatic: Soon bandits flared up again between Jiangshan and Yushan; within a week forty-eight of them had been captured and delivered.

sentences.zh: 終子秀之任，賊不復動，水潦所及，則爲治橋樑，修堰閘，補城壁，浚水原，助葺民廬，振以錢米，招通鄰糴。

translations.literal: Throughout Zixiu's tenure the robbers did not stir again; where floodwaters had reached, he had bridges repaired, sluice gates restored, city walls patched, water channels dredged, dwellings rebuilt for the people, relief given in cash and grain, and grain purchased from neighboring districts.
translations.idiomatic: For the rest of Zixiu's term the bandits stayed quiet. Wherever the floods had struck, he rebuilt bridges, repaired sluices, patched walls, dredged waterways, helped restore homes, distributed cash and grain, and bought grain from neighboring prefectures.

sentences.zh: 奏蠲秋苗萬五千石有奇，盡代納其夏稅，並除公私一切之負；

translations.literal: He memorialized to remit more than fifteen thousand shi of autumn grain tax, paid their summer levies in full on their behalf, and canceled every public and private debt;
translations.idiomatic: He secured remission of more than fifteen thousand shi of autumn grain tax, paid the summer levy for the people himself, and wiped out every public and private debt owed them;

sentences.zh: 坍溪沙壅之田，請於朝，永蠲其稅，民用復蘇。

translations.literal: for fields choked by collapsed embankments and sand buildup he petitioned the court for a permanent tax exemption, and common livelihood revived.
translations.idiomatic: for fields buried under collapsed dikes and silt he won a permanent tax exemption from the court, and life in the district recovered.

sentences.zh: 南渡後，孔子裔孫寓衢州，詔權以衢學奉祀，因循逾年，無專饗之廟。

translations.literal: After the southward relocation, a descendant of Confucius lived in Quzhou; an edict provisionally ordered the Quzhou school to maintain his sacrifices, but year after year dragged on with no dedicated temple for his rites.
translations.idiomatic: After the court moved south, a descendant of Confucius resided in Quzhou; an edict had the prefectural school maintain his sacrifices on a temporary basis, yet years passed with no temple devoted to his cult.

sentences.zh: 子秀撤廢佛寺，奏立家廟如闕里。

translations.literal: Zixiu demolished abandoned Buddhist temples and memorialized to establish a family temple like that at Queli.
translations.idiomatic: Zixiu tore down derelict Buddhist halls and petitioned to build a Confucian ancestral temple modeled on Queli.

sentences.zh: 既成，行釋菜禮。

translations.literal: When it was finished he performed the shicai offering ceremony.
translations.idiomatic: When the temple stood complete, he conducted the shicai offering rite.

sentences.zh: 以政最遷太常丞，以言罷。

translations.literal: For outstanding administration he was promoted to Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, then dismissed on account of remonstrance.
translations.idiomatic: Rated highest for his governance, he was promoted to vice director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, then removed after speaking too bluntly at court.

sentences.zh: 未幾，遷大宗正丞，遷金部郎官。

translations.literal: Before long he was moved to Vice Director of the Imperial Clan Court, then to Secretary of the Revenue Section.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly afterward he became vice director of the Imperial Clan Court, then secretary in the Revenue Section.

sentences.zh: 金部舊責州郡以必不可辨之泛數，吏顛倒爲奸欺。

translations.literal: The Revenue Section had long required prefectures and counties to supply indeterminate lump sums impossible to verify, and clerks turned this upside down into fraud.
translations.idiomatic: The Revenue Section had long demanded from each prefecture vague lump sums no one could audit, and clerks inverted the figures into systematic fraud.

sentences.zh: 子秀日夜討論，給冊轉遞以均其輸，人人如債切身，不遣一字而輸足。

translations.literal: Zixiu debated the matter day and night, issued registers for rotating delivery to equalize payments, made every man feel the debt as his own skin, and without pressing a single word the quotas were fully met.
translations.idiomatic: Zixiu worked the problem day and night, issued rotating delivery registers to spread the burden evenly, and made each payer feel the debt on his own skin—yet without a harsh word from him every quota was filled.

sentences.zh: 遷將作監、淮東總領，辭。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Director of Imperial Construction and Huaidong Chief Steward but declined.
translations.idiomatic: He was offered director of imperial construction and Huaidong chief steward, but declined both.

sentences.zh: 改知甯國府，辭。

translations.literal: He was reassigned as prefect of Ningguo Prefecture but declined again.
translations.idiomatic: He was reassigned to govern Ningguo Prefecture and declined again.

sentences.zh: 爲左司兼右司，再兼金部。

translations.literal: He served in the Left Section while also holding the Right Section, and again doubled as Revenue secretary.
translations.idiomatic: He held the Left Section while also filling the Right, and once more doubled as Revenue secretary.

sentences.zh: 與丞相丁大全議不合，去國。

translations.literal: He disagreed with the Grand Councilor Ding Daquan and left the capital.
translations.idiomatic: He fell out with Grand Councilor Ding Daquan and left the capital.

sentences.zh: 差知吉州，尋鐫罷。

translations.literal: He was appointed prefect of Jizhou and soon engraved-discharged.
translations.idiomatic: He was posted to Jizhou as prefect, then soon stripped of rank by engraved dismissal.

sentences.zh: 進大理少卿，直華文閣、浙東提點刑獄兼知婺州。

translations.literal: He advanced to Vice Director of the Court of Judicial Review, was made direct attendant of the Huawen Pavilion, Zhedong Judicial Intendant, and concurrently prefect of Wuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to vice director of the Court of Judicial Review, was made attendant of the Huawen Pavilion, Zhedong judicial intendant, and concurrently prefect of Wuzhou.

sentences.zh: 婺多勢家，有田連阡陌而無賦稅者，子秀悉核其田，書諸牘，勢家以爲厲己，嗾言者罷之。

translations.literal: Wuzhou had many powerful families with fields stretching across whole districts yet paying no tax; Zixiu audited all such lands and entered them in the registers; the powerful took this as an injury to themselves and incited remonstrators to have him dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Wuzhou teemed with powerful houses whose estates sprawled across whole districts yet paid no tax; Zixiu audited every such holding and entered it in the registers. The great families took this as a personal attack and set remonstrators on him until he was removed.

sentences.zh: 尋遷湖南轉運副使，以迎養非便辭，移浙西提點刑獄。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to Vice Transport Commissioner of Hunan but declined on grounds that receiving his parents there would be inconvenient; he was moved to Zhexi Judicial Intendant.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon named Hunan's vice transport commissioner but declined, saying it would be awkward to bring his parents there; he was shifted to Zhexi judicial intendant instead.

sentences.zh: 子秀冒暑周行八郡三十九縣，獄爲之清。

translations.literal: Zixiu braved the summer heat to tour eight prefectures and thirty-nine counties, and the prisons were cleared thereby.
translations.idiomatic: Zixiu toured eight prefectures and thirty-nine counties in the midsummer heat, and the jails emptied in his wake.

sentences.zh: 安吉州有婦人訴人殺其夫與二僕，郡守捐賞萬緡，逮系考掠十餘人，終莫得其實。

translations.literal: In Anji a woman accused someone of killing her husband and two servants; the prefect offered a reward of ten thousand strings of cash, arrested and tortured more than ten people, and still could not establish the truth.
translations.idiomatic: In Anji a woman charged that someone had murdered her husband and two servants; the prefect posted a ten-thousand-string reward, seized and tortured more than ten suspects, and still could not learn the truth.

sentences.zh: 子秀密訪之，乃婦人賂宗室子殺其夫，僕救之，並殺以滅口。

translations.literal: Zixiu investigated in secret and found that the woman had bribed an imperial-clan member to kill her husband; when the servants tried to save him they were killed as well to silence witnesses.
translations.idiomatic: Zixiu investigated quietly and found that the woman had paid an imperial clansman to kill her husband; when the servants tried to intervene, they too were murdered to silence them.

sentences.zh: 一問即伏誅，又釋偽會之連逮者，遠近稱爲神明。

translations.literal: One round of questioning and the culprits confessed and were executed; he also released those falsely implicated through association, and near and far hailed him as a spirit of justice.
translations.idiomatic: A single interrogation brought confession and execution; he also freed those swept up on false association charges, and people near and far called him uncannily just.

sentences.zh: 初，獄訟之滯，皆由期限之不應。

translations.literal: At first, the backlog in lawsuits stemmed entirely from failure to meet deadlines.
translations.idiomatic: At first every delay in the courts came from missed reporting deadlines.

sentences.zh: 使者下車，或親書戒州縣勿違，而違如故，則怒之。

translations.literal: When the commissioner took up his post he might personally write warnings to prefectures and counties not to violate them, yet violations continued as before—then he would grow angry.
translations.idiomatic: When a commissioner arrived he might personally write prefectures and counties not to miss the deadline; they missed it all the same, and he grew furious.

sentences.zh: 怒之，改匣，又違則又重怒之，至再三。

translations.literal: Angered, he would change the dispatch box; if they violated again he grew angrier still, even to a third round.
translations.idiomatic: In his anger he would change the dispatch box; if they missed again he raged again, and again, even a third time.

sentences.zh: 而專卒四出，巡尉等司繳限抱匣費不貲，則其勢必違。

translations.literal: Yet dedicated runners were sent everywhere; patrol officers and the like, bearing the deadline box and its costs, could not bear the expense—so violation was inevitable.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile dedicated runners scoured every district; patrol officers and the like, charged with carrying the deadline box, could not afford the cost—so missing the deadline was inevitable.

sentences.zh: 子秀與州縣約，到限者徑詣庭下，吏不得要索，亦無違者。

translations.literal: Zixiu made an agreement with prefectures and counties: when the deadline arrived they were to come straight to his hall, clerks might not demand bribes, and no one violated the rule.
translations.idiomatic: Zixiu struck a bargain with prefectures and counties: when the deadline came they were to appear directly in his hall, clerks were forbidden to extort fees—and no one was late.

sentences.zh: 其後創迴圈總匣屬各州主管官，凡管內諸司報應皆併入匣，一日一遣，公移則又總實於匣以往。

translations.literal: Afterward he created a rotating-ring master box assigned to each prefecture's chief officer; every report from offices under his jurisdiction was consolidated into the box and dispatched once a day; official communications were likewise sealed in summary form into the box and sent onward.
translations.idiomatic: He then devised a rotating master dispatch box for each prefecture's chief officer: every report from offices under his charge went into the box and went out once a day; routine documents were likewise summarized, sealed in the box, and forwarded.

sentences.zh: 於是事無小大，纖悉畢具，而風聞者反謂專卒淩州縣，劾罷之，子秀笑而已。

translations.literal: Thus matters great and small were recorded in fullest detail, yet those who traded in rumor accused his dedicated runners of bullying prefectures and counties, impeached him, and had him dismissed—Zixiu only smiled.
translations.idiomatic: Soon every matter, large or small, was on record in full detail—yet rumor-mongers accused his runners of bullying prefectures and counties, impeached him, and had him removed. Zixiu only smiled.

sentences.zh: 移江東提點刑獄。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Jiangdong Judicial Intendant.
translations.idiomatic: He was moved to Jiangdong judicial intendant.

sentences.zh: 度宗即位，進太常少卿兼右司，尋兼知臨安府，以言罷。

translations.literal: When Emperor Duzong ascended the throne, Zixiu was promoted to Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices while also holding the Right Section, then concurrently prefect of Lin'an, but was dismissed on account of remonstrance.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Duzong took the throne, Zixiu was made vice director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices with concurrent Right Section duties, then also prefect of Lin'an—only to be dismissed again after blunt remonstrance.

sentences.zh: 起知婺州，卒。

translations.literal: He was recalled as prefect of Wuzhou and died in office.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled to Wuzhou as prefect and died there.

sentences.zh: 子秀少從上虞劉漢弼游，磊落英發，抵掌極談，神采飛動。

translations.literal: In youth Zixiu studied under Liu Hanbi of Shangyu—open and spirited, clapping hands in fervent debate, his expression flying with animation.
translations.idiomatic: As a young man Zixiu studied with Liu Hanbi of Shangyu—bold, quick-spirited, slapping the table in heated talk, his face alive with energy.

sentences.zh: 與人交久而益親，死生患難，營救不遺力。

translations.literal: In friendship he grew closer the longer he knew someone; in life-or-death crisis he spared no effort to rescue.
translations.idiomatic: The longer he knew a friend, the closer they became; in life-or-death trouble he spent himself without reserve.

sentences.zh: 聞一善則手錄之。

translations.literal: When he heard of a good deed he copied it out by hand.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he heard of a worthy act he copied it out in his own hand.

sentences.zh: 李伯玉

translations.literal: Li Boyu
translations.idiomatic: Li Boyu

sentences.zh: 李伯玉，字純甫，饒州餘幹人。

translations.literal: Li Boyu, styled Chunfu, was a native of Yugan in Raozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Li Boyu, styled Chunfu, came from Yugan in Raozhou.

sentences.zh: 端平二年，進士第二。

translations.literal: In the second year of Duanping he placed second in the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Duanping (1235) he finished second on the jinshi rolls.

sentences.zh: 初名誠，以犯理宗潛諱更今名。

translations.literal: His original name was Cheng; because it violated Emperor Lizong's taboo name while he was still heir, he took his present name.
translations.idiomatic: He had first been named Cheng, but that clashed with Emperor Lizong's taboo name from his years as heir, so he adopted his present name.

sentences.zh: 授觀察推官、太學正兼莊文府教授、太學博士。

translations.literal: He was appointed surveillance investigating censor, Director of the Imperial Academy with concurrent appointment as lecturer at the Zhuangwen Palace, and Academy erudite.
translations.idiomatic: He was made surveillance investigating censor, director of the Imperial Academy with concurrent lectureship at the Zhuangwen Palace, and academy erudite.

sentences.zh: 召試館職，曆詆貴戚大臣，直聲暴起。

translations.literal: Called to trial appointment for a palace post, he repeatedly denounced noble kin and grand ministers, and his reputation for blunt integrity soared.
translations.idiomatic: Summoned to a trial appointment for a palace post, he denounced noble kin and senior ministers one after another, and his reputation for blunt integrity exploded overnight.

sentences.zh: 改校書郎，奏言：「台評迎合上意，論罷尤焴、楊棟、盧鉞三人，忠邪不辨，乞同罷。

translations.literal: Made collator, he memorialized: "The censorial reviewers curried imperial favor and impeached You Yu, Yang Dong, and Lu Qian; loyalty and treachery were not distinguished—I beg they be dismissed as well.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to collator, he memorialized: "The censorial reviewers have flattered the throne and driven out You Yu, Yang Dong, and Lu Qian without distinguishing loyal men from traitors—I ask that they be dismissed as well.

sentences.zh: 」帝不允。

translations.literal: " The emperor would not agree.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor refused.

sentences.zh: 監察御史陳垓連劾罷之。

translations.literal: Supervisory censor Chen Kai impeached him repeatedly until he was dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Supervisory censor Chen Kai impeached him again and again until he was removed.

sentences.zh: 奉雲台祠，差知南康軍，遷著作佐郎兼沂靖惠王府教授，兼考功郎官，兼尚書右司員外郎。

translations.literal: He received the Yuntai temple stipend, was assigned prefect of Nankang Circuit, promoted to Assistant Compiler with concurrent lectureship at the Yijinghui Prince's mansion, concurrent Secretary of the Merit Section, and concurrent Vice Director of the Right Section of the Imperial Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He took the Yuntai temple stipend, was posted as prefect of Nankang, then rose to assistant compiler with concurrent posts lecturing at the Yijinghui Prince's mansion, secretary in the Merit Section, and vice director in the Secretariat's Right Section.

sentences.zh: 引故事彈台臣蕭隸來，遷著作郎。

translations.literal: Citing precedent he impeached censor Xiao Lai—then was promoted to Compiler.
translations.idiomatic: Invoking precedent he impeached censor Xiao Lai—and was promoted to compiler.

sentences.zh: 帝怒，降兩官罷敘。

translations.literal: The emperor was furious; Boyu was reduced two ranks and barred from office sequence.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was enraged; Boyu was demoted two ranks and barred from further appointment.

sentences.zh: 復知邵武軍，改湖北提點刑獄，移福建，遷尚右郎官。

translations.literal: He was again made prefect of Shaowu Circuit, then Hubei Judicial Intendant, then moved to Fujian, and promoted to Secretary of the Right Section.
translations.idiomatic: He returned as prefect of Shaowu, became Hubei judicial intendant, was shifted to Fujian, and was promoted to secretary in the Right Section.

sentences.zh: 侍御史何夢然論伯玉乃吳潛之死黨，奉祀，遷福建提舉常平、淮西轉運判官。

translations.literal: Censor-in-waiting He Mengran argued that Boyu was a sworn partisan of the deceased Wu Qian; he was given temple stipend, then made Fujian Commissioner for Ever-Normal Granaries and Huaidong Transport Vice Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Censor-in-waiting He Mengran charged that Boyu had been a diehard follower of the late Wu Qian; he was given a temple stipend, then made Fujian ever-normal commissioner and Huaidong transport vice commissioner.

sentences.zh: 召赴經筵，遷考功郎兼太子侍讀，拜太府少卿、秘書少監、起居郎、工部侍郎。

translations.literal: Summoned to the classics lecture, he was made Merit Section secretary with concurrent Lecturer to the Crown Prince, then appointed Vice Director of the Court of the Imperial Treasury, Vice Director of the Imperial Library, Diarist, and Vice Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: Called to the classics lecture, he became Merit Section secretary and lecturer to the crown prince, then vice director of the Imperial Treasury, vice director of the Imperial Library, diarist, and vice minister of works.

sentences.zh: 度宗即位，兼侍講，權禮部侍郎，升兼同修國史、實錄院同修撰。

translations.literal: When Duzong took the throne, Boyu concurrently served as lecturer, Acting Vice Minister of Rites, and was elevated to joint compiler of the National History and Veritable Records.
translations.idiomatic: When Duzong ascended the throne, Boyu served concurrently as lecturer and acting vice minister of rites, and was elevated to joint compiler of the national history and veritable records.

sentences.zh: 賈似道嘗集百官議事，忽厲聲曰：「諸君非似道拔擢，安得至此！

translations.literal: Jia Sidao once assembled all officials to discuss affairs and suddenly shouted: "You gentlemen were not promoted by Sidao—how else would you have reached this place!
translations.idiomatic: Jia Sidao once gathered the officials to discuss policy and suddenly barked: "None of you reached your posts without Sidao's favor—how else would you be here!

sentences.zh: 」衆默然莫敢應者，伯玉答曰：「伯玉殿試第二名，平章不拔擢，伯玉地步亦可以至此。

translations.literal: " The crowd fell silent; none dared answer. Boyu replied: "Boyu placed second in the palace examination—even without the Grand Councilor's favor, Boyu's standing could have brought him here.
translations.idiomatic: " The hall went silent; no one answered. Boyu said: "Boyu placed second in the palace examination. Even without the grand councilor's patronage, Boyu's own merit could have brought him here.

sentences.zh: 」似道雖改容而有怒色。

translations.literal: " Sidao changed his manner but bore anger in his face.
translations.idiomatic: " Sidao smoothed his expression, but anger showed in his eyes.

sentences.zh: 既退，即治歸。

translations.literal: Once he withdrew, Boyu at once prepared to retire home.
translations.idiomatic: As soon as the session ended, Boyu began arranging his withdrawal from office.

sentences.zh: 以顯文閣待制知隆興府，右正言黃萬石論罷。

translations.literal: As awaiting-draft gentleman of the Xianwen Pavilion he was made prefect of Longxing; Right Remonstrator Huang Wanshi impeached him and he was dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: As Xianwen Pavilion awaiting-draft gentleman he governed Longxing; Right Remonstrator Huang Wanshi impeached him and he was removed.

sentences.zh: 召入覲，擢權禮部尚書兼侍讀。

translations.literal: Summoned for audience, he was elevated to Acting Minister of Rites with concurrent lectureship.
translations.idiomatic: Recalled to court, he was raised to acting minister of rites with concurrent lectureship.

sentences.zh: 似道益專國柄，帝以伯玉舊學，進之臥內，相對泣下，欲用以參大政，似道益忌之，而伯玉尋病卒。

translations.literal: Sidao grew ever more monopolistic of state power; the emperor, remembering Boyu as an old teacher, received him in the inner chamber—they wept face to face—the emperor wished to employ him in high policy, Sidao grew more jealous, and Boyu soon died of illness.
translations.idiomatic: Sidao tightened his grip on power. The emperor, remembering Boyu as an old teacher, received him in the inner chamber; they wept together, and the emperor meant to bring him into high policy—but Sidao grew more hostile, and Boyu soon died of illness.

sentences.zh: 伯玉嘗請罷童子科，以爲非所以成人材，厚風俗。

translations.literal: Boyu once petitioned to abolish the child-prodigy examination, holding that it was no way to mature talent or enrich custom.
translations.idiomatic: Boyu once asked to abolish the child-prodigy examination, arguing that it did not cultivate real talent or strengthen public morals.

sentences.zh: 趙汝騰嘗薦八士，各有品目，于伯玉曰「銅山鐵壁」。

translations.literal: Zhao Ruteng once recommended eight scholars, each with a rating; of Boyu he said "bronze mountain, iron rampart."
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Ruteng once nominated eight scholars, each with a verdict; of Boyu he wrote "a bronze mountain, an iron wall."

sentences.zh: 立朝風節，大較似之。

translations.literal: His bearing in court matched that likeness in the main.
translations.idiomatic: His conduct at court largely lived up to that praise.

sentences.zh: 所著有《斛峰集》。

translations.literal: His collected works are the Hufeng Ji.
translations.idiomatic: His writings survive as the *Hufeng Ji*.

sentences.zh: 論曰：陸持之學足以承其家，而不幸蚤喪，徐鹿卿論議明達，克施有政，趙逢龍之清操，汝騰之不撓，孫夢觀之平直，洪天錫、黃師雍、徐元傑、李伯玉皆悉心直言，不避權勢，孫子秀政績著見，皆當時之傑出云。

translations.literal: The commentary says: Lu Chizhi's learning sufficed to carry on his family line, yet he was unhappily cut off early; Xu Luqing's discourse was clear and penetrating and he succeeded in putting policy into practice; Zhao Fenglong's pure integrity, Ruteng's unyielding character, Sun Mengguan's straightforwardness, and Hong Tianxi, Huang Shiyong, Xu Yuanjie, and Li Boyu—all poured their hearts into blunt speech and did not shrink from power; Sun Zixiu's administrative achievements stood forth plainly; all were outstanding men of their age.
translations.idiomatic: The historians comment: Lu Chizhi's learning was enough to sustain his house, yet he died young; Xu Luqing spoke with clarity and put good government into practice; Zhao Fenglong's integrity, Ruteng's refusal to bend, Sun Mengguan's plain dealing, and Hong Tianxi, Huang Shiyong, Xu Yuanjie, and Li Boyu—all spoke their minds without fear of power; Sun Zixiu's record in office was plain for all to see. Each was a standout of his day.
